Its main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya like U. S. Automakers are based out of Detroit. It is also known as the birthplace of [[pachinko]].
As of [[2003]], the city has an estimated [[population]] of 2,190,549 and the [[population density|density]] of 6,710.21 persons per [[square kilometer|km&sup2]]. The total area is 326.45 km².
Nagoya is currently served by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki International Airport, NGO) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. [[Chubu International Airport]] (Centrair) will take over Nagoya's scheduled air services in 2005.
The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[cities designated by government ordinance|government ordinance]] and has the following ''[[ku]]'' (wards): [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]], [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]], [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]], [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]], [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]], [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]], [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]], [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]], [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]], [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]], [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]], [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]], [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]], [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]], [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]], and [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]].
[[Toyota]] is headquartered in nearby [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]], Aichi prefecture.
Nagoya’s famous sight seeing spots include ''[[Nagoya Castle|Nagoya-jō]]'' (名古屋城, [[Nagoya Castle]]) and ''Atsuta-jingu'' (熱田神宮, Atsuta Shrine). ''Nagoya-jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored to the original condition in 1959. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent ''Kin-no Shachi'' (金の鯱, Golden Killer Whales) on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta-jingu'' is known as the second- most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines ''Kusanagino-mitsurugi'' (草薙神剣, the Kusanagi sacred sward), one of the three holy treasures in Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,000 national treasures representing its 2,000 years’ history.

As of [[2003]], the city has an estimated [[population]] of 2,190,549 and the [[population density|density]] of 6,710.21 persons per [[square kilometer|km&sup2]]. The total area is 326.45 km².
==Administration==
The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[cities designated by government ordinance|government ordinance]] and has the following [[Wards of Japan|wards]] (''ku''): [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]], [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]], [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]], [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]], [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]], [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]], [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]], [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]], [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]], [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]], [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]], [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]], [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]], [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]], [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]], and [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]].
==Sightseeing==
Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include [[Nagoya Castle]] (名古屋城, Nagoya-jō) and [[Atsuta Shrine]] (熱田神宮, Atsuta Jingū).
''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored to the original condition in 1959. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent ''Kin no Shachi'' (金の鯱, Golden Killer Whales) on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya.
''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines ''[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]'' (草薙神剣, the Kusanagi sacred sword), one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,000 national treasures representing its 2,000 years' history.
==Transportation==
Nagoya is currently served by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki International Airport, NGO) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. [[Chubu International Airport]] (Centrair) will take over Nagoya's scheduled air services in 2005.
[[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tokaido Shinkansen]], [[Tokaido Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]]. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s.
==Economy==
Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya as U. S. automakers are based out of Detroit. [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area.
Nagoya is also known as the birthplace of [[pachinko]].

Located on the [[Pacific]] [[coast]] in the [[Chubu region]] on central [[Honshu]], it is the [[capital]] of [[Aichi Prefecture|Aichi]] [[prefecture]].
As of [[2003]], the city has an estimated [[population]] of 2,190,549 and the [[population density|density]] of 6,710.21 persons per [[square kilometer|km&sup2]]. The total area is 326.45 km².
==Administration==
The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[cities designated by government ordinance|government ordinance]] and has the following [[Wards of Japan|wards]] (''ku''): [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]], [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]], [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]], [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]], [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]], [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]], [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]], [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]], [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]], [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]], [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]], [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]], [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]], [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]], [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]], and [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]].
==Sightseeing==
Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include [[Nagoya Castle]] (名古屋城, Nagoya-jō) and [[Atsuta Shrine]] (熱田神宮, Atsuta Jingū).
''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored to the original condition in 1959. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent ''Kin no Shachi'' (金の鯱, Golden Killer Whales) on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya.
''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines ''[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]'' (草薙神剣, the Kusanagi sacred sword), one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,000 national treasures representing its 2,000 years' history.
==Transportation==
Nagoya is currently served by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki International Airport, NGO) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. [[Chubu International Airport]] (Centrair) will take over Nagoya's scheduled air services in 2005.
[[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tokaido Shinkansen]], [[Tokaido Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]]. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s.
==Economy==
Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya as U. S. automakers are based out of Detroit. [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area.
Nagoya is also known as the birthplace of [[pachinko]].

[[Image:Nagoyajou.jpg|frame|Nagoya Castle in June of 2004.]] '''Nagoya''' (名古屋市; -shi) is the fourth largest and the third most prosperous city in [[Japan]]. Located on the [[Pacific]] [[coast]] in the [[Chubu region]] on central [[Honshu]], it is the [[capital]] of [[Aichi Prefecture]].
As of [[2003]], the city has an estimated [[population]] of 2,190,549 and the [[population density|density]] of 6,710.21 persons per [[square kilometre|km²]]. The total area is 326.45 km².
==Administration==
The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[cities designated by government ordinance|government ordinance]] and has the following [[Wards of Japan|wards]] (''ku''): [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]], [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]], [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]], [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]], [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]], [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]], [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]], [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]], [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]], [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]], [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]], [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]], [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]], [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]], [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]], and [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]].
==Sightseeing==
Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include [[Nagoya Castle]] (名古屋城, Nagoya-jō) and [[Atsuta Shrine]] (熱田神宮, Atsuta Jingū).
''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored to the original condition in 1959. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent ''Kin no Shachi'' (金の鯱, Golden Killer Whales) on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya.
''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines ''[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]'' (草薙神剣, the Kusanagi sacred sword), one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,000 national treasures representing its 2,000 years' history.
==Transportation==
Nagoya is currently served by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki International Airport, NGO) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. [[Chubu International Airport]] (Centrair) will take over Nagoya's scheduled air services in 2005.
[[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tokaido Shinkansen]], [[Tokaido Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]]. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s.
==Economy==
Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya as U. S. automakers are based out of Detroit. [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. The Japanese [[confectionary]] company [[Marukawa]] is headquartered in Nagoya. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area.
Nagoya is also known as the birthplace of [[pachinko]].

''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent ''Kin no Shachi'' (金の鯱, Golden Killer Whales) on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya.
''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines ''[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]'' (草薙神剣, the Kusanagi sacred sword), one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. On [[February 17]],[[2005]], all of [[Nagoya Airport]]'s commerical flights moved to Chubu. [[Nagoya Airport]] is now a general aviation facility.
[[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tokaido Shinkansen]], [[Tokaido Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]]. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s.
== Economy == Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya as U. S. automakers are based out of Detroit. [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. The Japanese [[confectionary]] company [[Marukawa]] is headquartered in Nagoya. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area.
Nagoya is also known as the birthplace of [[pachinko]].

[[Image:Nagoyajou.jpg|frame|Nagoya Castle.]] '''Nagoya''' (名古屋市; -shi) is the fourth largest and the third most prosperous city in [[Japan]]. Located on the [[Pacific]] [[coast]] in the [[Chubu region]] on central [[Honshu]], it is the [[capital]] of [[Aichi Prefecture]]. == History == The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[cities designated by government ordinance|government ordinance]]. == Sightseeing == Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include [[Nagoya Castle]] (名古屋城, Nagoya-jō) and [[Atsuta Shrine]] (熱田神宮, Atsuta Jingū). ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored to the original condition in 1959. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent ''Kin no Shachi'' (金の鯱, Golden Carp) on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines ''[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]'' (草薙神剣, the Kusanagi sacred sword), one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 national treasures representing its 2,000 years' history. A modern attraction is the [[Nagoya TV Tower]] and JR Central Towers of [[Nagoya Station]]. == Wards == Nagoya has 16 [[Wards of Japan|wards]] (''ku''): * [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]] * [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]] * [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]] * [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]] * [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]] * [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]] * [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]] * [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]] * [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]] * [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]] * [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]] * [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]] * [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]] * [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]] * [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]] * [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]] == Demographics == As of [[2003]], the city has an estimated [[population]] of 2,190,549 and the [[population density|density]] of 6,710.21 persons per [[square kilometre|km²]]. The total area is 326.45 km². == Transportation == Nagoya is served by [[Chubu Centrair International Airport]] (NGO) in the city of [[Tokoname, Aichi|Tokoname]] and by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki Airport) (NKM) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. On [[February 17]],[[2005]], all of [[Nagoya Airport]]'s commerical flights (except for flights operated by [[J-Air]]) moved to Centrair. [[Nagoya Airport]] is now used as a [[general aviation]] and [[airbase]] facility. [[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tokaido Shinkansen]], [[Tokaido Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]]. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s. == Economy == Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya as U. S. automakers are based out of Detroit. [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. The Japanese [[confectionary]] company [[Marukawa]] is headquartered in Nagoya. [[Image:Nagoyajou.jpg|frame|Nagoya Castle.]] '''Nagoya''' (名古屋市; -shi) is the fourth largest and the third most prosperous city in [[Japan]]. Located on the [[Pacific]] [[coast]] in the [[Chubu region]] on central [[Honshu]], it is the [[capital]] of [[Aichi Prefecture]]. == History == The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[cities designated by government ordinance|government ordinance]]. == Sightseeing == Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include [[Nagoya Castle]] (名古屋城, Nagoya-jō) and [[Atsuta Shrine]] (熱田神宮, Atsuta Jingū). ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored to the original condition in 1959. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent ''Kin no Shachi'' (金の鯱, Golden Carp) on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines ''[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]'' (草薙神剣, the Kusanagi sacred sword), one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 national treasures representing its 2,000 years' history. A modern attraction is the [[Nagoya TV Tower]] and JR Central Towers of [[Nagoya Station]]. == Wards == Nagoya has 16 [[Wards of Japan|wards]] (''ku''): * [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]] * [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]] * [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]] * [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]] * [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]] * [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]] * [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]] * [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]] * [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]] * [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]] * [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]] * [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]] * [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]] * [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]] * [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]] * [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]] == Demographics == As of [[2003]], the city has an estimated [[population]] of 2,190,549 and the [[population density|density]] of 6,710.21 persons per [[square kilometre|km²]]. The total area is 326.45 km². == Transportation == Nagoya is served by [[Chubu Centrair International Airport]] (NGO) in the city of [[Tokoname, Aichi|Tokoname]] and by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki Airport) (NKM) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. On [[February 17]],[[2005]], all of [[Nagoya Airport]]'s commerical flights (except for flights operated by [[J-Air]]) moved to Centrair. [[Nagoya Airport]] is now used as a [[general aviation]] and [[airbase]] facility. [[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tokaido Shinkansen]], [[Tokaido Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]]. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s. == Economy == Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya as U. S. automakers are based out of Detroit. [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. The Japanese [[confectionary]] company [[Marukawa]] is headquartered in Nagoya. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area. Nagoya is also known as the birthplace of [[pachinko]]. [[Image:Nagoya Castle 01.jpg|thumb|300px|[[Nagoya Castle]]]] '''Nagoya''' (名古屋市; -shi) is the fourth largest (third largest metropolitan region) and the third most prosperous city in [[Japan]]. Located on the [[Pacific]] [[coast]] in the [[Chubu region]] on central [[Honshu]], it is the [[capital]] of [[Aichi Prefecture]]. == History == The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], and was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[cities designated by government ordinance|government ordinance]]. == Sightseeing == Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include [[Nagoya Castle]] (名古屋城, Nagoya-jō) and [[Atsuta Shrine]] (熱田神宮, Atsuta Jingū). ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored to the original condition in 1959. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent ''Kin no Shachi'' (金の鯱, Golden Carp) on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines ''[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]'' (草薙神剣, the Kusanagi sacred sword), one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 national treasures representing its 2,000 years' history. A modern attraction is the [[Nagoya TV Tower]] and JR Central Towers of [[Nagoya Station]]. == Wards == Nagoya has 16 [[Wards of Japan|wards]] (''ku''): * [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]] * [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]] * [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]] * [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]] * [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]] * [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]] * [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]] * [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]] * [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]] * [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]] * [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]] * [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]] * [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]] * [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]] * [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]] * [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]] == Demographics == As of [[2003]], the city has an estimated [[population]] of 2,190,549 and the [[population density|density]] of 6,710.21 persons per [[square kilometre|km²]]. The total area is 326.45 km². Its [[metropolitan area]] extends into [[Mie]] and [[Gifu]] prefectures, with approximately six million people, only Osaka and Tokyo being larger. == Transportation == Nagoya is served by [[Chubu Centrair International Airport]] (NGO) in the city of [[Tokoname, Aichi|Tokoname]] and by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki Airport) (NKM) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. On [[February 17]],[[2005]], all of [[Nagoya Airport]]'s commercial flights (except for flights operated by [[J-Air]]) moved to Centrair. [[Nagoya Airport]] is now used as a [[general aviation]] and [[airbase]] facility. [[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tokaido Shinkansen]], [[Tokaido Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]], among others. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s. == Economy == Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya as U. S. automakers are based out of Detroit. [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. The Japanese [[confectionary]] company [[Marukawa]] is headquartered in Nagoya, as is the fine ceramics company [[Noritake]]. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area. ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored to the original condition in 1959. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent ''Kin no Shachi'' (金の鯱, Golden Carp) on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines ''[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]'' (草薙神剣, the Kusanagi sacred sword), one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 national treasures representing its 2,000 years' history. A modern attraction is the [[Nagoya TV Tower]] and JR Central Towers of [[Nagoya Station]]. == Wards == Nagoya has 16 [[Wards of Japan|wards]] (''ku''): {| |- |valign=top| * [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]] * [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]] * [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]] * [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]] * [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]] * [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]] * [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]] * [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]] |valign=top| * [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]] * [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]] * [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]] * [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]] * [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]] * [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]] * [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]] * [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]] |} == Demographics == As of [[2003]], the city has an estimated [[population]] of 2,190,549 and the [[population density|density]] of 6,710.21 persons per [[square kilometre|km²]]. The total area is 326.45 km². Its [[metropolitan area]] extends into [[Mie]] and [[Gifu]] prefectures, with approximately six million people, only Osaka and Tokyo being larger. == Transportation == Nagoya is served by [[Chubu Centrair International Airport]] (NGO) in the city of [[Tokoname, Aichi|Tokoname]] and by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki Airport) (NKM) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. On [[February 17]],[[2005]], all of [[Nagoya Airport]]'s commercial flights (except for flights operated by [[J-Air]]) moved to Centrair. [[Nagoya Airport]] is now used as a [[general aviation]] and [[airbase]] facility. [[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tokaido Shinkansen]], [[Tokaido Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]], among others. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s. == Economy == Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya as U. S. automakers are based out of Detroit. [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. The Japanese [[confectionary]] company [[Marukawa]] is headquartered in Nagoya, as is the fine ceramics company [[Noritake]]. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area. Nagoya is also known as the birthplace of [[pachinko]]. '''Breakdown of Nagoya's [[Gross domestic product|GDP]] by economic activity'''
(from the 2005 city profile published by the City of Nagoya)

Manufacturing 12.3%

Administrative Services Supply 5.9%
Construction 5.8%
Finance and Insurance 5.4%
Others 3.7% Currently being held on the eastern hills of Nagoya in the neighboring cities of [[Nagakute, Aichi|Nagakute]] and [[Seto, Aichi|Seto]] is the [[World Expo 2005]], also known as Aichi Expo. Located on the [[Pacific]] [[coast]] in the [[Chubu region]] on central [[Honshu]], it is the [[capital]] of [[Aichi Prefecture]]. == History == The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], and was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[City designated by government ordinance (Japan)|government ordinance]]. == Sightseeing == Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include [[Nagoya Castle]] (名古屋城, Nagoya-jō) and [[Atsuta Shrine]] (熱田神宮, Atsuta Jingū). ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored to the original condition in 1959. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent ''Kin no Shachi'' (金の鯱, Golden Carp) on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines ''[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]'' (草薙神剣, the Kusanagi sacred sword), one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 national treasures representing its 2,000 years' history. On [[February 17]],[[2005]], all of [[Nagoya Airport]]'s commercial flights (except for flights operated by [[J-Air]]) moved to Centrair. [[Nagoya Airport]] is now used as a [[general aviation]] and [[airbase]] facility. [[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tokaido Shinkansen]], [[Tokaido Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]], among others. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s. == Economy == Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya as U. S. automakers are based out of Detroit. [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. The Japanese [[confectionary]] company [[Marukawa]] is headquartered in Nagoya, as is the fine ceramics company [[Noritake]]. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area. {{Japanese city| Name = Nagoya| JapaneseName = 名古屋| Region = [[Chubu|Chubu]]| Prefecture = [[Aichi prefecture]]| Area = 326.45 | Population = 2,190,549 | PopDate = 2003 | Density = 6,710.21 | Mayor = Takehisa Matsubara | Latitude = 35°07' N| Longitude = 136°56' E| Flower = [[Lilium]]| Tree = [[Camphor Laurel]]| SymbolImage=Nagoya_CitySymbol.png| CityHallPostalCode = 460-0001| CityHallAddress=Nagoya-shi, Sannomaru 3-chome, Naka-ku 1-1| CityHallPhone=052-972-2017| CityHallLink = [http://www.city.nagoya.jp/ Nagoya City] | CityMap=Map_Aichi_Nagoya_City.png| ExtraNotes= | }} [[Image:Nagoya Castle 01.jpg|thumb|300px|[[Nagoya Castle]]]] '''Nagoya''' (名古屋市; -shi) is the fourth largest (third largest metropolitan region) and the third most prosperous city in [[Japan]]. Located on the [[Pacific]] [[coast]] in the [[Chubu region]] on central [[Honshu]], it is the [[capital]] of [[Aichi Prefecture]]. == History == The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], and was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[City designated by government ordinance (Japan)|government ordinance]]. == Sightseeing == Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include [[Nagoya Castle]] (名古屋城, Nagoya-jō) and [[Atsuta Shrine]] (熱田神宮, Atsuta Jingū). ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored to its original condition in 1959. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent ''Kin no Shachi'' (金の鯱, Golden Orca) on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines ''[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]'' ((草薙神剣, the Kusanagi sacred sword), one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 national treasures representing its 2,000 years' history. Located on the [[Pacific]] [[coast]] in the [[Chubu region]] on central [[Honshu]], it is the [[capital]] of [[Aichi Prefecture]]. == History == The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], and was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[City designated by government ordinance (Japan)|government ordinance]]. == Sightseeing == Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include [[Nagoya Castle]] (名古屋城, Nagoya-jō) and [[Atsuta Shrine]] (熱田神宮, Atsuta Jingū). ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored to its original condition in 1959. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent ''Kin no Shachi'' (金の鯱, Golden Orca) on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines ''[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]'' ((草薙神剣, the Kusanagi sacred sword), one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 national treasures representing its 2,000 years' history. [[Nagoya Airport]] is now used as a [[general aviation]] and [[airbase]] facility. [[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tokaido Shinkansen]], [[Tokaido Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]], among others. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s. The city's name was historically written as 那古野 or 名護屋 (also read as ''Nagoya''), and as the city is located between [[Kyoto]] and [[Tokyo]], it was also historically known as ''Chūkyō'' (中京, "central capital"). == Sightseeing == Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include [[Nagoya Castle]] (名古屋城, Nagoya-jō) and [[Atsuta Shrine]] (熱田神宮, Atsuta Jingū). ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored to its original condition in 1959. Located on the [[Pacific]] [[coast]] in the [[Chūbu region]] on central [[Honshu]], it is the [[capital]] of [[Aichi Prefecture]]. == History == The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], and was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[City designated by government ordinance (Japan)|government ordinance]]. The city's name was historically written as 那古野 or 名護屋 (also read as ''Nagoya''), and as the city is located between [[Kyoto]] and [[Tokyo]], it was also historically known as ''Chūkyō'' (中京, "central capital"). == Sightseeing == [[Image:Nagoya Castle 01.jpg|thumb|left|[[Nagoya Castle]]]] Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include [[Nagoya Castle]] (名古屋城, Nagoya-jō) and [[Atsuta Shrine]] (熱田神宮, Atsuta Jingū). ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored to its original condition in 1959. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent ''Kin no Shachihoko'' (金の鯱, Golden Orca-like fish) on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines ''[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]'' ((草薙神剣, the Kusanagi sacred sword), one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 national treasures representing its 2,000 years' history. A modern attraction is the [[Nagoya TV Tower]] and JR Central Towers of [[Nagoya Station]]. == Wards == Nagoya has 16 [[Wards of Japan|wards]] (''ku''): {| |- |valign=top| * [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]] * [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]] * [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]] * [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]] * [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]] * [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]] * [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]] * [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]] |valign=top| * [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]] * [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]] * [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]] * [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]] * [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]] * [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]] * [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]] * [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]] |} == Demographics == As of [[2003]], the city has an estimated [[population]] of 2,190,549 and the [[population density|density]] of 6,710.21 persons per [[square kilometre|km²]]. The total area is 326.45 km². Its [[metropolitan area]] extends into [[Mie]] and [[Gifu]] prefectures, with approximately six million people, only Osaka and Tokyo being larger. == Transportation == [[Image:Surface Entrance to Shiyakusho Station (Nagoya-Japan).jpg|thumb|250px|Entrace to Shiyakusho Subway Station]] Nagoya is served by [[Chubu Centrair International Airport]] (NGO) in the city of [[Tokoname, Aichi|Tokoname]] and by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki Airport) (NKM) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. On [[February 17]],[[2005]], all of [[Nagoya Airport]]'s commercial flights (except for flights operated by [[J-Air]]) moved to Centrair. [[Nagoya Airport]] is now used as a [[general aviation]] and [[airbase]] facility. [[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tokaido Shinkansen]], [[Tokaido Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]], among others. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s. The city is also serviced by the [[Nagoya Subway]]. == Economy == [[Image:Nagoya_uitzicht.jpg|thumb|250px|An aerial view of Nagoya]] Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya as U. S. automakers are based out of Detroit. [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. The Japanese [[confectionery]] company [[Marukawa]] is headquartered in Nagoya, as is the fine ceramics company [[Noritake]]. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area. Nagoya is also known as the birthplace of [[pachinko]]. '''Breakdown of Nagoya's [[Gross domestic product|GDP]] by economic activity'''

The city's name was historically written as 那古野 or 名護屋 (also read as ''Nagoya''), and as the city is located between [[Kyoto]] and [[Tokyo]], it was also historically known as ''Chūkyō'' (中京, "central capital"). == Sightseeing == [[Image:Nagoya Castle 01.jpg|thumb|left|[[Nagoya Castle]]]] Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include [[Nagoya Castle]] (名古屋城, Nagoya-jō) and [[Atsuta Shrine]] (熱田神宮, Atsuta Jingū). ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored to its original condition in 1959. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent ''Kin no Shachihoko'' (金の鯱, Golden Orca-like fish) on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines ''[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]'' ((草薙神剣, the Kusanagi sacred sword), one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 national treasures representing its 2,000 years' history. A modern attraction is the [[Nagoya TV Tower]] and JR Central Towers of [[Nagoya Station]]. == Wards == Nagoya has 16 [[Wards of Japan|wards]] (''ku''): {| |- |valign=top| * [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]] * [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]] * [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]] * [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]] * [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]] * [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]] * [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]] * [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]] |valign=top| * [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]] * [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]] * [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]] * [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]] * [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]] * [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]] * [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]] * [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]] |} == Demographics == As of [[2003]], the city has an estimated [[population]] of 2,190,549 and the [[population density|density]] of 6,710.21 persons per [[square kilometre|km²]]. The total area is 326.45 km². Its [[metropolitan area]] extends into [[Mie]] and [[Gifu]] prefectures, with approximately six million people, only Osaka and Tokyo being larger. == Transportation == [[Image:Surface Entrance to Shiyakusho Station (Nagoya-Japan).jpg|thumb|250px|Entrace to Shiyakusho Subway Station]] Nagoya is served by [[Chubu Centrair International Airport]] (NGO) in the city of [[Tokoname, Aichi|Tokoname]] and by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki Airport) (NKM) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. On [[February 17]],[[2005]], all of [[Nagoya Airport]]'s commercial flights (except for flights operated by [[J-Air]]) moved to Centrair. [[Nagoya Airport]] is now used as a [[general aviation]] and [[airbase]] facility. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s. The city is also serviced by the [[Nagoya Subway]]. == Economy == [[Image:Nagoya_uitzicht.jpg|thumb|250px|An aerial view of Nagoya]] Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya as U. S. automakers are based out of Detroit. [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. The Japanese [[confectionery]] company [[Marukawa]] is headquartered in Nagoya, as is the fine ceramics company [[Noritake]]. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area. Located on the [[Pacific]] [[coast]] in the [[Chūbu region]] on central [[Honshu]], it is the [[capital]] of [[Aichi Prefecture]]. == History == The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], and was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[City designated by government ordinance (Japan)|government ordinance]]. The city's name was historically written as 那古野 or 名護屋 (also read as ''Nagoya''), and as the city is located between [[Kyoto]] and [[Tokyo]], it was also historically known as ''Chūkyō'' (中京, "central capital"). == Sightseeing == [[Image:Nagoya Castle 01.jpg|thumb|left|[[Nagoya Castle]]]] Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include [[Nagoya Castle]] (名古屋城, Nagoya-jō) and [[Atsuta Shrine]] (熱田神宮, Atsuta Jingū). ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored to its original condition in 1959. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent ''Kin no Shachihoko'' (金の鯱, Golden Orca-like fish) on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines ''[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]'' ((草薙神剣, the Kusanagi sacred sword), one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 national treasures representing its 2,000 years' history. A modern attraction is the [[Nagoya TV Tower]] and JR Central Towers of [[Nagoya Station]]. == Wards == Nagoya has 16 [[Wards of Japan|wards]] (''ku''): {| |- |valign=top| * [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]] * [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]] * [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]] * [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]] * [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]] * [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]] * [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]] * [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]] |valign=top| * [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]] * [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]] * [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]] * [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]] * [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]] * [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]] * [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]] * [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]] |} == Demographics == As of [[2003]], the city has an estimated [[population]] of 2,190,549 and the [[population density|density]] of 6,710.21 persons per [[square kilometre|km²]]. The total area is 326.45 km². Its [[metropolitan area]] extends into [[Mie]] and [[Gifu]] prefectures, with approximately six million people, only Osaka and Tokyo being larger. == Transportation == [[Image:Surface Entrance to Shiyakusho Station (Nagoya-Japan).jpg|thumb|250px|Entrace to Shiyakusho Subway Station]] Nagoya is served by [[Chubu Centrair International Airport]] (NGO) in the city of [[Tokoname, Aichi|Tokoname]] and by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki Airport) (NKM) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. On [[February 17]],[[2005]], all of [[Nagoya Airport]]'s commercial flights (except for flights operated by [[J-Air]]) moved to Centrair. [[Nagoya Airport]] is now used as a [[general aviation]] and [[airbase]] facility. [[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tokaido Shinkansen]], [[Tokaido Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]], among others. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s. The city is also serviced by the [[Nagoya Subway]]. == Economy == [[Image:Nagoya_uitzicht.jpg|thumb|250px|An aerial view of Nagoya]] Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya as U. S. automakers are based out of Detroit. [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. The Japanese [[confectionery]] company [[Marukawa]] is headquartered in Nagoya, as is the fine ceramics company [[Noritake]]. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area. Nagoya is also known as the birthplace of [[pachinko]]. '''Breakdown of Nagoya's [[Gross domestic product|GDP]] by economic activity'''

Sannomaru 3-chome, Naka-ku 1-1| CityHallPhone=052-972-2017| CityHallLink = [http://www.city.nagoya.jp/ Nagoya City] | MapImage=| ExtraNotes= | }} '''Nagoya''' (名古屋市; -shi) is the fourth largest (third largest metropolitan region) and the third most prosperous city in [[Japan]]. Located on the [[Pacific]] [[coast]] in the [[Chūbu region]] on central [[Honshu]], it is the [[capital]] of [[Aichi Prefecture]]. == History == The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], and was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[City designated by government ordinance (Japan)|government ordinance]]. The city's name was historically written as 那古野 or 名護屋 (also read as ''Nagoya''), and as the city is located between [[Kyoto]] and [[Tokyo]], it was also historically known as ''Chūkyō'' (中京, "central capital"). == Sightseeing == [[Image:Nagoya Castle 01.jpg|thumb|left|[[Nagoya Castle]]]] Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include [[Nagoya Castle]] (名古屋城, Nagoya-jō) and [[Atsuta Shrine]] (熱田神宮, Atsuta Jingū). ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored to its original condition in 1959. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent ''Kin no Shachihoko'' (金の鯱, Golden Orca-like fish) on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines ''[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]'' ((草薙神剣, the Kusanagi sacred sword), one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 national treasures representing its 2,000 years' history. A modern attraction is the [[Nagoya TV Tower]] and JR Central Towers of [[Nagoya Station]]. == Wards == Nagoya has 16 [[Wards of Japan|wards]] (''ku''): {| |- |valign=top| * [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]] * [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]] * [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]] * [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]] * [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]] * [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]] * [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]] * [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]] |valign=top| * [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]] * [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]] * [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]] * [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]] * [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]] * [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]] * [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]] * [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]] |} == Demographics == As of [[2003]], the city has an estimated [[population]] of 2,190,549 and the [[population density|density]] of 6,710.21 persons per [[square kilometre|km²]]. The total area is 326.45 km². Its [[metropolitan area]] extends into [[Mie]] and [[Gifu]] prefectures, with approximately six million people, only Osaka and Tokyo being larger. == Transportation == [[Image:Surface Entrance to Shiyakusho Station (Nagoya-Japan).jpg|thumb|250px|Entrace to Shiyakusho Subway Station]] Nagoya is served by [[Chubu Centrair International Airport]] (NGO) in the city of [[Tokoname, Aichi|Tokoname]] and by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki Airport) (NKM) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. On [[February 17]],[[2005]], all of [[Nagoya Airport]]'s commercial flights (except for flights operated by [[J-Air]]) moved to Centrair. [[Nagoya Airport]] is now used as a [[general aviation]] and [[airbase]] facility. [[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tokaido Shinkansen]], [[Tokaido Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]], among others. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s. The city is also serviced by the [[Nagoya Subway]]. == Economy == [[Image:Nagoya_uitzicht.jpg|thumb|250px|An aerial view of Nagoya]] Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya as U. S. automakers are based out of Detroit. [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. The Japanese [[confectionery]] company [[Marukawa]] is headquartered in Nagoya, as is the fine ceramics company [[Noritake]]. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area. Nagoya is also known as the birthplace of [[pachinko]]. '''Breakdown of Nagoya's [[Gross domestic product|GDP]] by economic activity'''

{{Japanese city| Name = Nagoya City| JapaneseName = 名古屋市| Region = [[Chūbu region|Chūbu]], [[Tokai region|Tokai]]| Prefecture = [[Aichi prefecture]]| Area = 326.45 | Population = 2,190,549 | PopDate = 2003 | Density = 6,710.21 | Mayor = Takehisa Matsubara | Coord = {{coor dm|35|07|N|136|56|E|type:city_region:JP}}| Flower = [[Lilium]]| Tree = [[Camphor Laurel]]| SymbolImage=Nagoya_CitySymbol.png| CityHallPostalCode = 460-0001| CityHallAddress=Nagoya-shi,
Naka-ku, Sannomaru 3-chome 1-1| CityHallPhone=052-972-2017| CityHallLink = [http://www.city.nagoya.jp/ Nagoya City] | MapImage=Nagoya.png| ExtraNotes= | }} '''Nagoya''' (名古屋市; -shi) is the fourth largest (third largest metropolitan region) and the third most prosperous city in [[Japan]]. Located on the [[Pacific]] [[coast]] in the [[Chūbu region]] on central [[Honshu]], it is the [[capital]] of [[Aichi Prefecture]]. == History == The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], and was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[City designated by government ordinance (Japan)|government ordinance]]. The city's name was historically written as 那古野 or 名護屋 (also read as ''Nagoya''), and as the city is located between [[Kyoto]] and [[Tokyo]], it was also historically known as ''Chūkyō'' (中京, "central capital"). == Sightseeing == [[Image:Nagoya Castle 01.jpg|thumb|left|[[Nagoya Castle]]]] Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include [[Nagoya Castle]] (名古屋城, Nagoya-jō) and [[Atsuta Shrine]] (熱田神宮, Atsuta Jingū). [[Nagoya Castle]] ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored in 1959, though some modern amenities such as elevators were added. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent ''Kin no Shachihoko'' (金の鯱, Golden Orca) on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines ''[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]'' ((草薙神剣, the Kusanagi sacred sword), one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 national treasures representing its 2,000 years' history. A modern attraction is the [[Nagoya TV Tower]] and JR Central Towers of [[Nagoya Station]]. == Wards == Nagoya has 16 [[Wards of Japan|wards]] (''ku''): {| |- |valign=top| * [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]] * [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]] * [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]] * [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]] * [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]] * [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]] * [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]] * [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]] |valign=top| * [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]] * [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]] * [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]] * [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]] * [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]] * [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]] * [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]] * [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]] |} == Demographics == As of [[2003]], the city has an estimated [[population]] of 2,190,549 and the [[population density|density]] of 6,710.21 persons per [[square kilometre|km²]]. The total area is 326.45 km². Its [[Chukyo Metropolitan Area|metropolitan area]] extends into [[Mie]] and [[Gifu]] prefectures, with a total population of about 9 million people, with only Osaka and Tokyo being larger. == Transportation == [[Image:Surface Entrance to Shiyakusho Station (Nagoya-Japan).jpg|thumb|250px|Entrace to Shiyakusho Subway Station]] Nagoya is served by [[Chubu Centrair International Airport]] (NGO) in the city of [[Tokoname, Aichi|Tokoname]] and by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki Airport) (NKM) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. On [[February 17]],[[2005]], all of [[Nagoya Airport]]'s commercial flights (except for flights operated by [[J-Air]]) moved to Centrair. [[Nagoya Airport]] is now used as a [[general aviation]] and [[airbase]] facility. [[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tokaido Shinkansen]], [[Tokaido Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]], among others. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s. The city is also serviced by the [[Nagoya Subway]]. == Economy == [[Image:Nagoya_uitzicht.jpg|thumb|250px|An aerial view of Nagoya]] Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya as U. S. automakers are based out of Detroit. [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. The Japanese [[confectionery]] company [[Marukawa]] is headquartered in Nagoya, as is the fine ceramics company [[Noritake]]. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area. Nagoya is also known as the birthplace of [[pachinko]]. '''Breakdown of Nagoya's [[Gross domestic product|GDP]] by economic activity'''

{{Japanese city| Name = Nagoya City| JapaneseName = 名古屋市| Region = [[Chūbu region|Chūbu]], [[Tokai region|Tokai]]| Prefecture = [[Aichi prefecture]]| Area = 326.45 | Population = 2,190,549 | PopDate = 2003 | Density = 6,710.21 | Mayor = Takehisa Matsubara | Coord = {{coor dm|35|07|N|136|56|E|type:city_region:JP}}| Flower = [[Lilium]]| Tree = [[Camphor Laurel]]| SymbolImage=Nagoya_CitySymbol.png| CityHallPostalCode = 460-0001| CityHallAddress=Nagoya-shi,
Naka-ku, Sannomaru 3-chome 1-1| CityHallPhone=052-972-2017| CityHallLink = [http://www.city.nagoya.jp/ Nagoya City] | MapImage=Nagoya.png| ExtraNotes= | }} {{nihongo|'''Nagoya'''|名古屋市|nagoya-shi}} is the fourth largest (third largest metropolitan region) and the third most prosperous city in [[Japan]]. Located on the [[Pacific]] [[coast]] in the [[Chūbu region]] on central [[Honshu]], it is the [[capital]] of [[Aichi Prefecture]]. == History == The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], and was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[City designated by government ordinance (Japan)|government ordinance]]. The city's name was historically written as 那古野 or 名護屋 (also read as ''Nagoya''), and as the city is located between [[Kyoto]] and [[Tokyo]], it was also historically known as {{nihongo|"central capital"|中京|Chūkyō}}. == Sightseeing == [[Image:Nagoya Castle 01.jpg|thumb|left|[[Nagoya Castle]]]] Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include {{nihongo|[[Nagoya Castle]]|名古屋城|Nagoya-jō}} and {{nihongo|[[Atsuta Shrine]]|熱田神宮|Atsuta Jingū}}. [[Nagoya Castle]] ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored in 1959, though some modern amenities such as elevators were added. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent {{nihongo|Golden Orca|金の鯱|Kin no Shachihoko}} on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines {{nihongo|the Kusanagi sacred sword|草薙神剣|[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]}} one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 national treasures representing its 2,000 years' history. A modern attraction is the [[Nagoya TV Tower]] and JR Central Towers of [[Nagoya Station]]. == Wards == Nagoya has 16 {{nihongo|[[Wards of Japan|wards]]|''ku''|区}}: {| |- |valign=top| * [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]] * [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]] * [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]] * [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]] * [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]] * [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]] * [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]] * [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]] |valign=top| * [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]] * [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]] * [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]] * [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]] * [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]] * [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]] * [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]] * [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]] |} == Demographics == As of [[2003]], the city has an estimated [[population]] of 2,190,549 and the [[population density|density]] of 6,710.21 persons per [[square kilometre|km²]]. The total area is 326.45 km². Its [[Chukyo Metropolitan Area|metropolitan area]] extends into [[Mie]] and [[Gifu]] prefectures, with a total population of about 9 million people, with only Osaka and Tokyo being larger. == Transportation == [[Image:Surface Entrance to Shiyakusho Station (Nagoya-Japan).jpg|thumb|250px|Entrace to Shiyakusho Subway Station]] Nagoya is served by [[Chubu Centrair International Airport]] (NGO) in the city of [[Tokoname, Aichi|Tokoname]] and by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki Airport) (NKM) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. On [[February 17]],[[2005]], all of [[Nagoya Airport]]'s commercial flights (except for flights operated by [[J-Air]]) moved to Centrair. [[Nagoya Airport]] is now used as a [[general aviation]] and [[airbase]] facility. [[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tokaido Shinkansen]], [[Tokaido Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]], among others. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s. The city is also serviced by the [[Nagoya Subway]]. == Economy == [[Image:Nagoya_uitzicht.jpg|thumb|250px|An aerial view of Nagoya]] Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya as U. S. automakers are based out of Detroit. [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. The Japanese [[confectionery]] company [[Marukawa]] is headquartered in Nagoya, as is the fine ceramics company [[Noritake]]. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area. Nagoya is also known as the birthplace of [[pachinko]]. '''Breakdown of Nagoya's [[Gross domestic product|GDP]] by economic activity'''

The event was held from March 25 to September 25, 2005. == Sports== Nagoya is home to several professional sports teams. {| class="wikitable" |- ! scope="col" | Club ! scope="col" | Sport ! scope="col" | League ! scope="col" | Venue ! scope="col" | Established |- | [[Chunichi Dragons]] | [[Baseball]] | [[Central League]] | [[Nagoya Dome]] | [[1936]] |- | [[Nagoya Grampus Eight]] | [[Football (soccer)|Football]] | [[J. Naka-ku, Sannomaru 3-chome 1-1| CityHallPhone=052-972-2017| CityHallLink = [http://www.city.nagoya.jp/ Nagoya City] | MapImage=Nagoya.png| ExtraNotes= | }} {{nihongo|'''Nagoya'''|名古屋市|nagoya-shi}} is the fourth largest (third largest metropolitan region) and the third most prosperous city in [[Japan]]. Located on the [[Pacific]] [[coast]] in the [[Chūbu region]] on central [[Honshu]], it is the [[capital]] of [[Aichi Prefecture]]. == History == The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], and was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[City designated by government ordinance (Japan)|government ordinance]]. The city's name was historically written as 那古野 or 名護屋 (also read as ''Nagoya''), and as the city is located between [[Kyoto]] and [[Tokyo]], it was also historically known as {{nihongo|"central capital"|中京|Chūkyō}}. == Sightseeing == [[Image:Nagoya Castle 01.jpg|thumb|left|[[Nagoya Castle]]]] Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include {{nihongo|[[Nagoya Castle]]|名古屋城|Nagoya-jō}} and {{nihongo|[[Atsuta Shrine]]|熱田神宮|Atsuta Jingū}}. [[Nagoya Castle]] ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored in 1959, though some modern amenities such as elevators were added. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent {{nihongo|Golden Orca|金の鯱|Kin no Shachihoko}} on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines {{nihongo|the Kusanagi sacred sword|草薙神剣|[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]}} one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 national treasures representing its 2,000 years' history. Modern attractions include the [[Nagoya TV Tower]] and JR Central Towers of [[Nagoya Station]]. == Wards == Nagoya has 16 {{nihongo|[[Wards of Japan|wards]]|''ku''|区}}: {| |- |valign=top| * [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]] * [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]] * [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]] * [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]] * [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]] * [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]] * [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]] * [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]] |valign=top| * [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]] * [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]] * [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]] * [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]] * [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]] * [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]] * [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]] * [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]] |} == Demographics == As of [[2003]], the city has an estimated [[population]] of 2,190,549 and the [[population density|density]] of 6,710.21 persons per [[square kilometre|km²]]. The total area is 326.45 km². Its [[Chukyo Metropolitan Area|metropolitan area]] extends into [[Mie]] and [[Gifu]] prefectures, with a total population of about 9 million people, with only Osaka and Tokyo being larger. == Transportation == [[Image:Surface Entrance to Shiyakusho Station (Nagoya-Japan).jpg|thumb|250px|Entrace to Shiyakusho Subway Station]] Nagoya is served by [[Chubu Centrair International Airport]] (NGO) in the city of [[Tokoname, Aichi|Tokoname]] and by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki Airport) (NKM) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. On [[February 17]],[[2005]], all of [[Nagoya Airport]]'s commercial flights (except for flights operated by [[J-Air]]) moved to Centrair. [[Nagoya Airport]] is now used as a [[general aviation]] and [[airbase]] facility. [[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tokaido Shinkansen]], [[Tokaido Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]], among others. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s. The city is also serviced by the [[Nagoya Subway]]. == Economy == [[Image:Nagoya_uitzicht.jpg|thumb|250px|An aerial view of Nagoya]] Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya as U. S. automakers are based out of Detroit. [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. The Japanese [[confectionery]] company [[Marukawa]] is headquartered in Nagoya, as is the fine ceramics company [[Noritake]]. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area. Nagoya is also known as the birthplace of [[pachinko]]. '''Breakdown of Nagoya's [[Gross domestic product|GDP]] by economic activity'''

The event was held from March 25 to September 25, 2005. == Sports== Nagoya is home to several professional sports teams. {| class="wikitable" |- ! scope="col" | Club ! scope="col" | Sport ! scope="col" | League ! scope="col" | Venue ! scope="col" | Established |- | [[Chunichi Dragons]] | [[Baseball]] | [[Central League]] | [[Nagoya Dome]] | [[1936]] |- | [[Nagoya Grampus Eight]] | [[Football (soccer)|Football]] | [[J. {{Japanese city| Name = Nagoya City| JapaneseName = 名古屋市| Region = [[Chūbu region|Chūbu]], [[Tokai region|Tokai]]| Prefecture = [[Aichi prefecture]]| Area = 326.45 | Population = 2,190,549 | PopDate = 2003 | Density = 6,710.21 | Mayor = Takehisa Matsubara | Coord = {{coor dm|35|07|N|136|56|E|type:city_region:JP}}| Flower = [[Lilium]]| Tree = [[Camphor Laurel]]| SymbolImage=Nagoya_CitySymbol.png| CityHallPostalCode = 460-0001| CityHallAddress=Nagoya-shi,
Naka-ku, Sannomaru 3-chome 1-1| CityHallPhone=052-972-2017| CityHallLink = [http://www.city.nagoya.jp/ Nagoya City] | MapImage=Map Nagoya en.png| ExtraNotes= | }} {{nihongo|'''Nagoya'''|名古屋市|nagoya-shi}} is the fourth largest (third largest metropolitan region) and the third most prosperous city in [[Japan]]. Located on the [[Pacific]] [[coast]] in the [[Chūbu region]] on central [[Honshu]], it is the [[capital]] of [[Aichi Prefecture]]. == History == The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], and was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[City designated by government ordinance (Japan)|government ordinance]]. The city's name was historically written as 那古野 or 名護屋 (also read as ''Nagoya''), and as the city is located between [[Kyoto]] and [[Tokyo]], it was also historically known as {{nihongo|"central capital"|中京|Chūkyō}}. == Sightseeing == [[Image:Nagoya Castle 01.jpg|thumb|left|[[Nagoya Castle]]]] Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include {{nihongo|[[Nagoya Castle]]|名古屋城|Nagoya-jō}} and {{nihongo|[[Atsuta Shrine]]|熱田神宮|Atsuta Jingū}}. [[Nagoya Castle]] ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored in 1959, though some modern amenities such as elevators were added. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent {{nihongo|Golden Orca|金の鯱|Kin no Shachihoko}} on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines {{nihongo|the Kusanagi sacred sword|草薙神剣|[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]}} one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 national treasures representing its 2,000 years' history. Modern attractions include the [[Nagoya TV Tower]] and JR Central Towers of [[Nagoya Station]]. == Wards == Nagoya has 16 {{nihongo|[[Wards of Japan|wards]]|''ku''|区}}: {| |- |valign=top| * [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]] * [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]] * [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]] * [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]] * [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]] * [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]] * [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]] * [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]] |valign=top| * [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]] * [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]] * [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]] * [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]] * [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]] * [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]] * [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]] * [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]] |} == Demographics == As of [[2003]], the city has an estimated [[population]] of 2,190,549 and the [[population density|density]] of 6,710.21 persons per [[square kilometre|km²]]. The total area is 326.45 km². Its [[Chukyo Metropolitan Area|metropolitan area]] extends into [[Mie]] and [[Gifu]] prefectures, with a total population of about 9 million people, with only Osaka and Tokyo being larger. == Transportation == [[Image:Surface Entrance to Shiyakusho Station (Nagoya-Japan).jpg|thumb|250px|Entrace to Shiyakusho Subway Station]] Nagoya is served by [[Chubu Centrair International Airport]] (NGO) in the city of [[Tokoname, Aichi|Tokoname]] and by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki Airport) (NKM) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. On [[February 17]],[[2005]], all of [[Nagoya Airport]]'s commercial flights (except for flights operated by [[J-Air]]) moved to Centrair. [[Nagoya Airport]] is now used as a [[general aviation]] and [[airbase]] facility. [[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tokaido Shinkansen]], [[Tokaido Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]], among others. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s. The city is also serviced by the [[Nagoya Subway]]. == Economy == [[Image:Nagoya_uitzicht.jpg|thumb|250px|An aerial view of Nagoya]] Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya as U. S. automakers are based out of Detroit. [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. The Japanese [[confectionery]] company [[Marukawa]] is headquartered in Nagoya, as is the fine ceramics company [[Noritake]]. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area. Nagoya is also known as the birthplace of [[pachinko]]. '''Breakdown of Nagoya's [[Gross domestic product|GDP]] by economic activity'''

The event was held from March 25 to September 25, 2005. == Sports== Nagoya is home to several professional sports teams. {| class="wikitable" |- ! scope="col" | Club ! scope="col" | Sport ! scope="col" | League ! scope="col" | Venue ! scope="col" | Established |- | [[Chunichi Dragons]] | [[Baseball]] | [[Central League]] | [[Nagoya Dome]] | [[1936]] |- | [[Nagoya Grampus Eight]] | [[Football (soccer)|Football]] | [[J. {{Japanese city| Name = Nagoya City| JapaneseName = 名古屋市| Region = [[Chūbu region|Chūbu]], [[Tokai region|Tokai]]| Prefecture = [[Aichi prefecture]]| Area = 326.45 | Population = 2,190,549 | PopDate = 2003 | Density = 6,710.21 | Mayor = Takehisa Matsubara | Coord = {{coor dm|35|07|N|136|56|E|type:city_region:JP}}| Flower = [[Lilium]]| Tree = [[Camphor Laurel]]| SymbolImage=Nagoya_CitySymbol.png| CityHallPostalCode = 460-0001| CityHallAddress=Nagoya-shi,
Naka-ku, Sannomaru 3-chome 1-1| CityHallPhone=052-972-2017| CityHallLink = [http://www.city.nagoya.jp/ Nagoya City] | MapImage=Map Nagoya en.png| ExtraNotes= | }} {{nihongo|'''Nagoya'''|名古屋市|nagoya-shi}} is the fourth largest (third largest metropolitan region) and the third most prosperous city in [[Japan]]. Located on the [[Pacific]] [[coast]] in the [[Chūbu region]] on central [[Honshu]], it is the [[capital]] of [[Aichi Prefecture]]. == History == The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], and was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[City designated by government ordinance (Japan)|government ordinance]]. The city's name was historically written as 那古野 or 名護屋 (also read as ''Nagoya''), and as the city is located between [[Kyoto]] and [[Tokyo]], it was also historically known as {{nihongo|"central capital"|中京|Chūkyō}}. == Sightseeing == [[Image:Nagoya Castle 01.jpg|thumb|left|[[Nagoya Castle]]]] Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include {{nihongo|[[Nagoya Castle]]|名古屋城|Nagoya-jō}} and {{nihongo|[[Atsuta Shrine]]|熱田神宮|Atsuta Jingū}}. [[Nagoya Castle]] ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored in 1959, though some modern amenities such as elevators were added. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent {{nihongo|Golden Orca|金の鯱|Kin no Shachihoko}} on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines {{nihongo|the Kusanagi sacred sword|草薙神剣|[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]}} one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 national treasures representing its 2,000 years' history. Modern attractions include the [[Nagoya TV Tower]] and JR Central Towers of [[Nagoya Station]]. == Wards == Nagoya has 16 {{nihongo|[[Wards of Japan|wards]]|''ku''|区}}: {| |- |valign=top| * [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]] * [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]] * [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]] * [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]] * [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]] * [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]] * [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]] * [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]] |valign=top| * [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]] * [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]] * [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]] * [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]] * [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]] * [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]] * [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]] * [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]] |} == Demographics == As of [[2003]], the city has an estimated [[population]] of 2,190,549 and the [[population density|density]] of 6,710.21 persons per [[square kilometre|km²]]. The total area is 326.45 km². Its [[Chukyo Metropolitan Area|metropolitan area]] extends into [[Mie]] and [[Gifu]] prefectures, with a total population of about 9 million people, with only Osaka and Tokyo being larger. == Transportation == [[Image:Surface Entrance to Shiyakusho Station (Nagoya-Japan).jpg|thumb|250px|Entrace to Shiyakusho Subway Station]] Nagoya is served by [[Chubu Centrair International Airport]] (NGO) in the city of [[Tokoname, Aichi|Tokoname]] and by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki Airport) (NKM) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. On [[February 17]],[[2005]], all of [[Nagoya Airport]]'s commercial flights (except for flights operated by [[J-Air]]) moved to Centrair. [[Nagoya Airport]] is now used as a [[general aviation]] and [[airbase]] facility. [[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tokaido Shinkansen]], [[Tokaido Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]], among others. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s. The city is also serviced by the [[Nagoya Subway]]. == Economy == [[Image:Nagoya_uitzicht.jpg|thumb|250px|An aerial view of Nagoya]] [[Image:Nagoya_IdcN.jpg|thumb|left|International design center NAGOYA (IdcN)]] Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya (akin to U.S. automakers being based out of [[Detroit, Michigan|Detroit]]). [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. The Japanese [[confectionery]] company [[Marukawa]] is headquartered in Nagoya, as is the fine ceramics company [[Noritake]]. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area. Nagoya is also known as the birthplace of [[pachinko]]. '''Breakdown of Nagoya's [[Gross domestic product|GDP]] by economic activity'''

The event was held from March 25 to September 25, 2005. == Sports== Nagoya is home to several professional sports teams. {| class="wikitable" |- ! scope="col" | Club ! scope="col" | Sport ! scope="col" | League ! scope="col" | Venue ! scope="col" | Established |- | [[Chunichi Dragons]] | [[Baseball]] | [[Central League]] | [[Nagoya Dome]] | [[1936]] |- | [[Nagoya Grampus Eight]] | [[Football (soccer)|Football]] | [[J.
