Naka-ku, Sannomaru 3-chome 1-1| CityHallPhone=052-972-2017| CityHallLink = [http://www.city.nagoya.jp/ Nagoya City] | MapImage=Map Nagoya en.png| ExtraNotes= | }} {{nihongo|'''Nagoya'''|名古屋市|nagoya-shi}} is the fourth largest (third largest metropolitan region) and the third most prosperous city in [[Japan]]. Located on the [[Pacific]] [[coast]] in the [[Chūbu region]] on central [[Honshu]], it is the [[capital]] of [[Aichi Prefecture]] and is one of Japan's major [[seaport|port]]s along with those of [[Tokyo]], [[Osaka]], [[Kobe]], [[Hakata-ku, Fukuoka|Hakata]], [[Yokohama]] and [[Chiba]]. == History == The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], and was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[City designated by government ordinance (Japan)|government ordinance]]. The city's name was historically written as 那古野 or 名護屋 (also read as ''Nagoya''), and as the city is located between [[Kyoto]] and [[Tokyo]], it was also historically known as {{nihongo|"central capital"|中京|Chūkyō}}. == Sightseeing == [[Image:Nagoya Castle 01.jpg|thumb|left|[[Nagoya Castle]]]] Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include {{nihongo|[[Nagoya Castle]]|名古屋城|Nagoya-jō}} and {{nihongo|[[Atsuta Shrine]]|熱田神宮|Atsuta Jingū}}. [[Nagoya Castle]] ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored in 1959, though some modern amenities such as elevators were added. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent {{nihongo|Golden Orca|金の鯱|Kin no Shachihoko}} on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines {{nihongo|the Kusanagi sacred sword|草薙神剣|[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]}} one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 national treasures representing its 2,000 years' history. Modern attractions include the [[Nagoya TV Tower]] and JR Central Towers of [[Nagoya Station]]. == Wards == Nagoya has 16 {{nihongo|[[Wards of Japan|wards]]|''ku''|区}}: {| |- |valign=top| * [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]] * [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]] * [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]] * [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]] * [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]] * [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]] * [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]] * [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]] |valign=top| * [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]] * [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]] * [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]] * [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]] * [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]] * [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]] * [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]] * [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]] |} == Demographics == As of [[2003]], the city has an estimated [[population]] of 2,190,549 and the [[population density|density]] of 6,710.21 persons per [[square kilometre|km²]]. The total area is 326.45 km². Its [[Chukyo Metropolitan Area|metropolitan area]] extends into [[Mie]] and [[Gifu]] prefectures, with a total population of about 9 million people, with only Osaka and Tokyo being larger. == Transportation == [[Image:Surface Entrance to Shiyakusho Station (Nagoya-Japan).jpg|thumb|250px|Entrace to Shiyakusho Subway Station]] Nagoya is served by [[Chubu Centrair International Airport]] (NGO) in the city of [[Tokoname, Aichi|Tokoname]] and by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki Airport) (NKM) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. On [[February 17]],[[2005]], all of [[Nagoya Airport]]'s commercial flights (except for flights operated by [[J-Air]]) moved to Centrair. [[Nagoya Airport]] is now used as a [[general aviation]] and [[airbase]] facility. [[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tokaido Shinkansen]], [[Tokaido Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]], among others. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s. The city is also serviced by the [[Nagoya Subway]]. == Economy == [[Image:Nagoya_uitzicht.jpg|thumb|250px|An aerial view of Nagoya]] [[Image:Nagoya_IdcN.jpg|thumb|left|International design center NAGOYA (IdcN)]] Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya (akin to U.S. automakers being based out of [[Detroit, Michigan|Detroit]]). [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. The Japanese [[confectionery]] company [[Marukawa]] is headquartered in Nagoya, as is the fine ceramics company [[Noritake]]. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area. Nagoya is also known as the birthplace of [[pachinko]]. '''Breakdown of Nagoya's [[Gross domestic product|GDP]] by economic activity'''

{{Japanese city| Name = Nagoya City| JapaneseName = 名古屋市| Region = [[Chūbu region|Chūbu]], [[Tokai region|Tokai]]| Prefecture = [[Aichi prefecture]]| Area = 326.45 | Population = 2,190,549 | PopDate = 2003 | Density = 6,710.21 | Mayor = Takehisa Matsubara | Coord = {{coor dm|35|07|N|136|56|E|type:city_region:JP}}| Flower = [[Lilium]]| Tree = [[Camphor Laurel]]| SymbolImage=Nagoya_CitySymbol.png| CityHallPostalCode = 460-0001| CityHallAddress=Nagoya-shi,
Naka-ku, Sannomaru 3-chome 1-1| CityHallPhone=052-972-2017| CityHallLink = [http://www.city.nagoya.jp/ Nagoya City] | MapImage=Map Nagoya en.png| ExtraNotes= | }} {{nihongo|'''Nagoya'''|名古屋市|nagoya-shi}} is the fourth largest (third largest metropolitan region) and the third most prosperous city in [[Japan]]. Located on the [[Pacific]] [[coast]] in the [[Chūbu region]] on central [[Honshu]], it is the [[capital]] of [[Aichi Prefecture]] and is one of Japan's major [[seaport|port]]s along with those of [[Tokyo]], [[Osaka]], [[Kobe]], [[Hakata-ku, Fukuoka|Hakata]], [[Yokohama]] and [[Chiba]]. == History == The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], and was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[City designated by government ordinance (Japan)|government ordinance]]. The city's name was historically written as 那古野 or 名護屋 (also read as ''Nagoya''), and as the city is located between [[Kyoto]] and [[Tokyo]], it was also historically known as {{nihongo|"central capital"|中京|Chūkyō}}. == Sightseeing == [[Image:Nagoya Castle 01.jpg|thumb|left|[[Nagoya Castle]]]] Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include {{nihongo|[[Nagoya Castle]]|名古屋城|Nagoya-jō}} and {{nihongo|[[Atsuta Shrine]]|熱田神宮|Atsuta Jingū}}. [[Nagoya Castle]] ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored in 1959, though some modern amenities such as elevators were added. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent {{nihongo|Golden Orca|金の鯱|Kin no Shachihoko}} on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines {{nihongo|the Kusanagi sacred sword|草薙神剣|[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]}} one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 [[national treasure]]s representing its 2,000 years' history. Modern attractions include the [[Nagoya TV Tower]] and JR Central Towers of [[Nagoya Station]]. == Wards == Nagoya has 16 {{nihongo|[[Wards of Japan|wards]]|''ku''|区}}: {| |- |valign=top| * [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]] * [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]] * [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]] * [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]] * [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]] * [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]] * [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]] * [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]] |valign=top| * [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]] * [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]] * [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]] * [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]] * [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]] * [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]] * [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]] * [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]] |} == Demographics == As of [[2003]], the city has an estimated [[population]] of 2,190,549 and the [[population density|density]] of 6,710.21 persons per [[square kilometre|km²]]. The total area is 326.45 km². Its [[Chukyo Metropolitan Area|metropolitan area]] extends into [[Mie]] and [[Gifu]] prefectures, with a total population of about 9 million people, with only Osaka and Tokyo being larger. == Transportation == [[Image:Surface Entrance to Shiyakusho Station (Nagoya-Japan).jpg|thumb|250px|Entrace to Shiyakusho Subway Station]] Nagoya is served by [[Chubu Centrair International Airport]] (NGO) in the city of [[Tokoname, Aichi|Tokoname]] and by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki Airport) (NKM) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. On [[February 17]],[[2005]], all of [[Nagoya Airport]]'s commercial flights (except for flights operated by [[J-Air]]) moved to Centrair. [[Nagoya Airport]] is now used as a [[general aviation]] and [[airbase]] facility. [[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tokaido Shinkansen]], [[Tokaido Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]], among others. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s. The city is also serviced by the [[Nagoya Subway]]. == Economy == [[Image:Nagoya_uitzicht.jpg|thumb|250px|An aerial view of Nagoya]] [[Image:Nagoya_IdcN.jpg|thumb|left|International design center NAGOYA (IdcN)]] Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya (akin to U.S. automakers being based out of [[Detroit, Michigan|Detroit]]). [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. The Japanese [[confectionery]] company [[Marukawa]] is headquartered in Nagoya, as is the fine ceramics company [[Noritake]]. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area. Nagoya is also known as the birthplace of [[pachinko]]. '''Breakdown of Nagoya's [[Gross domestic product|GDP]] by economic activity'''
(from the 2005 city profile published by the City of Nagoya) *Service 26% *Wholesale and Retail 20.2% *Manufacturing 12.3% *Shipping and Communications 10.4% *Real Estate 9.8% *Administrative Services Supply 5.9% *Construction 5.8% *Finance and Insurance 5.4% *Others 3.7% The [[World Expo 2005]], also known as Aichi Expo was held in the eastern hills of Nagoya in the neighboring cities of [[Nagakute, Aichi|Nagakute]] and [[Seto, Aichi|Seto]]. The event was held from March 25 to September 25, 2005. == Sports== Nagoya is home to several professional sports teams. {| class="wikitable" |- ! scope="col" | Club ! scope="col" | Sport ! scope="col" | League ! scope="col" | Venue ! scope="col" | Established |- | [[Chunichi Dragons]] | [[Baseball]] | [[Central League]] | [[Nagoya Dome]] | [[1936]] |- | [[Nagoya Grampus Eight]] | [[Football (soccer)|Football]] | [[J. {{Japanese city| Name = Nagoya City| JapaneseName = 名古屋市| Region = [[Chūbu region|Chūbu]], [[Tokai region|Tokai]]| Prefecture = [[Aichi prefecture]]| Area = 326.45 | Population = 2,190,549 | PopDate = 2003 | Density = 6,710.21 | Mayor = Takehisa Matsubara | Coord = {{coor dm|35|07|N|136|56|E|type:city_region:JP}}| Flower = [[Lilium]]| Tree = [[Camphor Laurel]]| SymbolImage=Nagoya_CitySymbol.png| CityHallPostalCode = 460-0001| CityHallAddress=Nagoya-shi,
Naka-ku, Sannomaru 3-chome 1-1| CityHallPhone=052-972-2017| CityHallLink = [http://www.city.nagoya.jp/ Nagoya City] | MapImage=Map Nagoya en.png| ExtraNotes= | }} {{nihongo|'''Nagoya'''|名古屋市|nagoya-shi}} is the fourth largest (third largest metropolitan region) and the third most prosperous city in [[Japan]]. Located on the [[Pacific]] [[coast]] in the [[Chūbu region]] on central [[Honshu]], it is the [[capital]] of [[Aichi Prefecture]] and is one of Japan's major [[seaport|port]]s along with those of [[Tokyo]], [[Osaka]], [[Kobe]], [[Hakata-ku, Fukuoka|Hakata]], [[Yokohama]] and [[Chiba]]. == History == The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], and was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[City designated by government ordinance (Japan)|government ordinance]]. The city's name was historically written as 那古野 or 名護屋 (also read as ''Nagoya''), and as the city is located between [[Kyoto]] and [[Tokyo]], it was also historically known as {{nihongo|"central capital"|中京|Chūkyō}}. == Sightseeing == [[Image:Nagoya Castle 01.jpg|thumb|left|[[Nagoya Castle]]]] Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include {{nihongo|[[Nagoya Castle]]|名古屋城|Nagoya-jō}} and {{nihongo|[[Atsuta Shrine]]|熱田神宮|Atsuta Jingū}}. [[Nagoya Castle]] ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored in 1959, though some modern amenities such as elevators were added. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent {{nihongo|Golden Orca|金の鯱|Kin no Shachihoko}} on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines {{nihongo|the Kusanagi sacred sword|草薙神剣|[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]}} one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 [[national treasure]]s representing its 2,000 years' history. Modern attractions include the [[Nagoya TV Tower]] and JR Central Towers of [[Nagoya Station]]. == Wards == Nagoya has 16 {{nihongo|[[Wards of Japan|wards]]|''ku''|区}}: {| |- |valign=top| * [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]] * [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]] * [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]] * [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]] * [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]] * [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]] * [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]] * [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]] |valign=top| * [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]] * [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]] * [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]] * [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]] * [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]] * [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]] * [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]] * [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]] |} == Demographics == As of [[2003]], the city has an estimated [[population]] of 2,190,549 and the [[population density|density]] of 6,710.21 persons per [[square kilometre|km²]]. The total area is 326.45 km². Its [[Chukyo Metropolitan Area|metropolitan area]] extends into [[Mie]] and [[Gifu]] prefectures, with a total population of about 9 million people, with only Osaka and Tokyo being larger. == Transportation == [[Image:Surface Entrance to Shiyakusho Station (Nagoya-Japan).jpg|thumb|250px|Entrace to Shiyakusho Subway Station]] Nagoya is served by [[Chubu Centrair International Airport]] (NGO) in the city of [[Tokoname, Aichi|Tokoname]] and by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki Airport) (NKM) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. On [[February 17]],[[2005]], all of [[Nagoya Airport]]'s commercial flights (except for flights operated by [[J-Air]]) moved to Centrair. [[Nagoya Airport]] is now used as a [[general aviation]] and [[airbase]] facility. [[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tokaido Shinkansen]], [[Tokaido Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]], among others. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s. The city is also serviced by the [[Nagoya Subway]]. == Economy == [[Image:Nagoya_uitzicht.jpg|thumb|250px|An aerial view of Nagoya]] [[Image:Nagoya_IdcN.jpg|thumb|left|International design center NAGOYA (IdcN)]] Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya (akin to U.S. automakers being based out of [[Detroit, Michigan|Detroit]]). [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. The Japanese [[confectionery]] company [[Marukawa]] is headquartered in Nagoya, as is the fine ceramics company [[Noritake]]. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area. Nagoya is also known as the birthplace of [[pachinko]]. '''Breakdown of Nagoya's [[Gross domestic product|GDP]] by economic activity'''

The event was held from March 25 to September 25, 2005. == Sports== Nagoya is home to several professional sports teams. {| class="wikitable" |- ! scope="col" | Club ! scope="col" | Sport ! scope="col" | League ! scope="col" | Venue ! scope="col" | Established |- | [[Chunichi Dragons]] | [[Baseball]] | [[Central League]] | [[Nagoya Dome]] | [[1936]] |- | [[Nagoya Grampus Eight]] | [[Football (soccer)|Football]] | [[J. {{Japanese city| Name = Nagoya City| JapaneseName = 名古屋市| Region = [[Chūbu region|Chūbu]], [[Tokai region|Tokai]]| Prefecture = [[Aichi prefecture]]| Area = 326.45 | Population = 2,190,549 | PopDate = 2003 | Density = 6,710.21 | Mayor = Takehisa Matsubara | Coord = {{coor dm|35|07|N|136|56|E|type:city_region:JP}}| Flower = [[Lilium]]| Tree = [[Camphor Laurel]]| SymbolImage=Nagoya_CitySymbol.png| CityHallPostalCode = 460-0001| CityHallAddress=Nagoya-shi,
Naka-ku, Sannomaru 3-chome 1-1| CityHallPhone=052-972-2017| CityHallLink = [http://www.city.nagoya.jp/ Nagoya City] | MapImage=Map Nagoya en.png| ExtraNotes= | }} {{nihongo|'''Nagoya'''|名古屋市|nagoya-shi}} is the fourth largest and the third most prosperous city in [[Japan]]. Located on the [[Pacific]] [[coast]] in the [[Chūbu region]] on central [[Honshu]], it is the [[capital]] of [[Aichi Prefecture]] and is one of Japan's major [[seaport|port]]s along with those of [[Tokyo]], [[Osaka]], [[Kobe]], [[Hakata-ku, Fukuoka|Hakata]], [[Yokohama]] and [[Chiba]]. It is also the center of Japan's third largest metropolitan region, known as the [[Chukyo Metropolitan Area]]. == History == The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], and was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[City designated by government ordinance (Japan)|government ordinance]]. The city's name was historically written as 那古野 or 名護屋 (also read as ''Nagoya''), and as the city is located between [[Kyoto]] and [[Tokyo]], it was also historically known as {{nihongo|"central capital"|中京|Chūkyō}}. == Sightseeing == [[Image:Nagoya Castle 01.jpg|thumb|left|[[Nagoya Castle]]]] Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include {{nihongo|[[Nagoya Castle]]|名古屋城|Nagoya-jō}} and {{nihongo|[[Atsuta Shrine]]|熱田神宮|Atsuta Jingū}}. [[Nagoya Castle]] ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored in 1959, though some modern amenities such as elevators were added. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent {{nihongo|Golden Orca|金の鯱|Kin no Shachihoko}} on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines {{nihongo|the Kusanagi sacred sword|草薙神剣|[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]}} one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 [[national treasure]]s representing its 2,000 years' history. Modern attractions include the [[Nagoya TV Tower]] and JR Central Towers of [[Nagoya Station]]. == Wards == Nagoya has 16 {{nihongo|[[Wards of Japan|wards]]|''ku''|区}}: {| |- |valign=top| * [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]] * [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]] * [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]] * [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]] * [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]] * [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]] * [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]] * [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]] |valign=top| * [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]] * [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]] * [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]] * [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]] * [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]] * [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]] * [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]] * [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]] |} == Demographics == As of [[2003]], the city has an estimated [[population]] of 2,190,549 and the [[population density|density]] of 6,710.21 persons per [[square kilometre|km²]]. The total area is 326.45 km². Its [[Chukyo Metropolitan Area|metropolitan area]] extends into [[Mie]] and [[Gifu]] prefectures, with a total population of about 9 million people, with only Osaka and Tokyo being larger. == Transportation == [[Image:Surface Entrance to Shiyakusho Station (Nagoya-Japan).jpg|thumb|250px|Entrace to Shiyakusho Subway Station]] Nagoya is served by [[Chubu Centrair International Airport]] (NGO) in the city of [[Tokoname, Aichi|Tokoname]] and by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki Airport) (NKM) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. On [[February 17]],[[2005]], all of [[Nagoya Airport]]'s commercial flights (except for flights operated by [[J-Air]]) moved to Centrair. [[Nagoya Airport]] is now used as a [[general aviation]] and [[airbase]] facility. [[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tokaido Shinkansen]], [[Tokaido Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]], among others. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s. The city is also serviced by the [[Nagoya Subway]]. == Economy == [[Image:Nagoya_uitzicht.jpg|thumb|250px|An aerial view of Nagoya]] [[Image:Nagoya_IdcN.jpg|thumb|left|International design center NAGOYA (IdcN)]] Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya (akin to U.S. automakers being based out of [[Detroit, Michigan|Detroit]]). [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. The Japanese [[confectionery]] company [[Marukawa]] is headquartered in Nagoya, as is the fine ceramics company [[Noritake]]. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area. Nagoya is also known as the birthplace of [[pachinko]]. '''Breakdown of Nagoya's [[Gross domestic product|GDP]] by economic activity'''
(from the 2005 city profile published by the City of Nagoya) *Service 26% *Wholesale and Retail 20.2% *Manufacturing 12.3% *Shipping and Communications 10.4% *Real Estate 9.8% *Administrative Services Supply 5.9% *Construction 5.8% *Finance and Insurance 5.4% *Others 3.7% The [[World Expo 2005]], also known as Aichi Expo was held in the eastern hills of Nagoya in the neighboring cities of [[Nagakute, Aichi|Nagakute]] and [[Seto, Aichi|Seto]]. The event was held from March 25 to September 25, 2005. == Sports== Nagoya is home to several professional sports teams. {| class="wikitable" |- ! scope="col" | Club ! scope="col" | Sport ! scope="col" | League ! scope="col" | Venue ! scope="col" | Established |- | [[Chunichi Dragons]] | [[Baseball]] | [[Central League]] | [[Nagoya Dome]] | [[1936]] |- | [[Nagoya Grampus Eight]] | [[Football (soccer)|Football]] | [[J. Located on the [[Pacific]] [[coast]] in the [[Chūbu region]] on central [[Honshu]], it is the [[capital]] of [[Aichi Prefecture]] and is one of Japan's major [[seaport|port]]s along with those of [[Tokyo]], [[Yokohama]], [[Osaka]], [[Kobe]], [[Chiba]], and[[Hakata-ku, Fukuoka|Hakata]]. It is also the center of Japan's third largest metropolitan region, known as the [[Chukyo Metropolitan Area]]. == History == The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], and was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[City designated by government ordinance (Japan)|government ordinance]]. The city's name was historically written as 那古野 or 名護屋 (also read as ''Nagoya''), and as the city is located between [[Kyoto]] and [[Tokyo]], it was also historically known as {{nihongo|"central capital"|中京|Chūkyō}}. == Sightseeing == [[Image:Nagoya Castle 01.jpg|thumb|left|[[Nagoya Castle]]]] Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include {{nihongo|[[Nagoya Castle]]|名古屋城|Nagoya-jō}} and {{nihongo|[[Atsuta Shrine]]|熱田神宮|Atsuta Jingū}}. [[Nagoya Castle]] ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored in 1959, though some modern amenities such as elevators were added. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent {{nihongo|Golden Orca|金の鯱|Kin no Shachihoko}} on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines {{nihongo|the Kusanagi sacred sword|草薙神剣|[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]}} one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 [[national treasure]]s representing its 2,000 years' history. Modern attractions include the [[Nagoya TV Tower]] and JR Central Towers of [[Nagoya Station]]. == Wards == Nagoya has 16 {{nihongo|[[Wards of Japan|wards]]|''ku''|区}}: {| |- |valign=top| * [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]] * [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]] * [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]] * [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]] * [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]] * [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]] * [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]] * [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]] |valign=top| * [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]] * [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]] * [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]] * [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]] * [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]] * [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]] * [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]] * [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]] |} == Demographics == As of [[2003]], the city has an estimated [[population]] of 2,190,549 and the [[population density|density]] of 6,710.21 persons per [[square kilometre|km²]]. The total area is 326.45 km². Its [[Chukyo Metropolitan Area|metropolitan area]] extends into [[Mie]] and [[Gifu]] prefectures, with a total population of about 9 million people, with only Osaka and Tokyo being larger. == Transportation == [[Image:Surface Entrance to Shiyakusho Station (Nagoya-Japan).jpg|thumb|250px|Entrace to Shiyakusho Subway Station]] Nagoya is served by [[Chubu Centrair International Airport]] (NGO) in the city of [[Tokoname, Aichi|Tokoname]] and by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki Airport) (NKM) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. On [[February 17]],[[2005]], all of [[Nagoya Airport]]'s commercial flights (except for flights operated by [[J-Air]]) moved to Centrair. [[Nagoya Airport]] is now used as a [[general aviation]] and [[airbase]] facility. [[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tokaido Shinkansen]], [[Tokaido Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]], among others. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s. The city is also serviced by the [[Nagoya Subway]]. == Economy == [[Image:Nagoya_uitzicht.jpg|thumb|250px|An aerial view of Nagoya]] [[Image:Nagoya_IdcN.jpg|thumb|left|International design center NAGOYA (IdcN)]] Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya (akin to U.S. automakers being based out of [[Detroit, Michigan|Detroit]]). [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. The Japanese [[confectionery]] company [[Marukawa]] is headquartered in Nagoya, as is the fine ceramics company [[Noritake]]. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area. Nagoya is also known as the birthplace of [[pachinko]]. '''Breakdown of Nagoya's [[Gross domestic product|GDP]] by economic activity'''

Naka-ku, Sannomaru 3-chome 1-1| CityHallPhone=052-972-2017| CityHallLink = [http://www.city.nagoya.jp/ Nagoya City] | MapImage=Map Nagoya en.png| ExtraNotes= | }} {{nihongo|'''Nagoya'''|名古屋市|nagoya-shi}} is the fourth largest and the third most prosperous city in [[Japan]]. Located on the [[Pacific]] [[coast]] in the [[Chūbu region]] on central [[Honshu]], it is the [[capital]] of [[Aichi Prefecture]] and is one of Japan's major [[seaport|port]]s along with those of [[Tokyo]], [[Osaka]], [[Kobe]], [[Yokohama]], [[Chiba]], and [[Hakata-ku, Fukuoka|Hakata]]. It is also the center of Japan's third largest metropolitan region, known as the [[Chukyo Metropolitan Area]]. == History == The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], and was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[City designated by government ordinance (Japan)|government ordinance]]. The city's name was historically written as 那古野 or 名護屋 (also read as ''Nagoya''), and as the city is located between [[Kyoto]] and [[Tokyo]], it was also historically known as {{nihongo|"central capital"|中京|Chūkyō}}. == Sightseeing == [[Image:Nagoya Castle 01.jpg|thumb|left|[[Nagoya Castle]]]] Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include {{nihongo|[[Nagoya Castle]]|名古屋城|Nagoya-jō}} and {{nihongo|[[Atsuta Shrine]]|熱田神宮|Atsuta Jingū}}. [[Nagoya Castle]] ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored in 1959, though some modern amenities such as elevators were added. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent {{nihongo|Golden Orca|金の鯱|Kin no Shachihoko}} on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines {{nihongo|the Kusanagi sacred sword|草薙神剣|[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]}} one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 [[national treasure]]s representing its 2,000 years' history. Modern attractions include the [[Nagoya TV Tower]] and JR Central Towers of [[Nagoya Station]]. == Wards == Nagoya has 16 {{nihongo|[[Wards of Japan|wards]]|''ku''|区}}: {| |- |valign=top| * [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]] * [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]] * [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]] * [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]] * [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]] * [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]] * [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]] * [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]] |valign=top| * [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]] * [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]] * [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]] * [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]] * [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]] * [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]] * [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]] * [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]] |} == Demographics == As of [[2003]], the city has an estimated [[population]] of 2,190,549 and the [[population density|density]] of 6,710.21 persons per [[square kilometre|km²]]. The total area is 326.45 km². Its [[Chukyo Metropolitan Area|metropolitan area]] extends into [[Mie]] and [[Gifu]] prefectures, with a total population of about 9 million people, with only Osaka and Tokyo being larger. == Transportation == [[Image:Surface Entrance to Shiyakusho Station (Nagoya-Japan).jpg|thumb|250px|Entrace to Shiyakusho Subway Station]] Nagoya is served by [[Chubu Centrair International Airport]] (NGO) in the city of [[Tokoname, Aichi|Tokoname]] and by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki Airport) (NKM) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. On [[February 17]],[[2005]], all of [[Nagoya Airport]]'s commercial flights (except for flights operated by [[J-Air]]) moved to Centrair. [[Nagoya Airport]] is now used as a [[general aviation]] and [[airbase]] facility. [[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tokaido Shinkansen]], [[Tokaido Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]], among others. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s. The city is also serviced by the [[Nagoya Subway]]. == Economy == [[Image:Nagoya_uitzicht.jpg|thumb|250px|An aerial view of Nagoya]] [[Image:Nagoya_IdcN.jpg|thumb|left|International design center NAGOYA (IdcN)]] Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya (akin to U.S. automakers being based out of [[Detroit, Michigan|Detroit]]). [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. The Japanese [[confectionery]] company [[Marukawa]] is headquartered in Nagoya, as is the fine ceramics company [[Noritake]]. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area. Nagoya is also known as the birthplace of [[pachinko]]. '''Breakdown of Nagoya's [[Gross domestic product|GDP]] by economic activity'''

Naka-ku, Sannomaru 3-chome 1-1| CityHallPhone=052-972-2017| CityHallLink = [http://www.city.nagoya.jp/ Nagoya City] | MapImage=Map Nagoya en.png| ExtraNotes= | }} {{nihongo|'''Nagoya'''|名古屋市|nagoya-shi}} is the fourth largest and the third most prosperous city in [[Japan]]. Located on the [[Pacific]] [[coast]] in the [[Chūbu region]] on central [[Honshu]], it is the [[capital]] of [[Aichi Prefecture]] and is one of Japan's major [[seaport|port]]s along with those of [[Tokyo]], [[Osaka]], [[Kobe]], [[Yokohama]], [[Chiba]], and [[Hakata-ku, Fukuoka|Hakata]]. It is also the center of Japan's third largest metropolitan region, known as the [[Chukyo Metropolitan Area]]. == History == The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], and was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[City designated by government ordinance (Japan)|government ordinance]]. The city's name was historically written as 那古野 or 名護屋 (also read as ''Nagoya''), and as the city is located between [[Kyoto]] and [[Tokyo]], it was also historically known as {{nihongo|"central capital"|中京|Chūkyō}}. == Sightseeing == [[Image:Nagoya Castle 01.jpg|thumb|left|[[Nagoya Castle]]]] Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include {{nihongo|[[Nagoya Castle]]|名古屋城|Nagoya-jō}} and {{nihongo|[[Atsuta Shrine]]|熱田神宮|Atsuta Jingū}}. [[Nagoya Castle]] ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored in 1959, though some modern amenities such as elevators were added. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent {{nihongo|Golden Orca|金の鯱|Kin no Shachihoko}} on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines {{nihongo|the Kusanagi sacred sword|草薙神剣|[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]}} one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 [[national treasure]]s representing its 2,000 years' history. Modern attractions include the [[Nagoya TV Tower]] and JR Central Towers of [[Nagoya Station]]. The total area is 326.45 km². Its [[Chukyo Metropolitan Area|metropolitan area]] extends into [[Mie]] and [[Gifu]] prefectures, with a total population of about 9 million people, with only Osaka and Tokyo being larger. == Transportation == [[Image:Surface Entrance to Shiyakusho Station (Nagoya-Japan).jpg|thumb|250px|Entrace to Shiyakusho Subway Station]] Nagoya is served by [[Chubu Centrair International Airport]] (NGO) in the city of [[Tokoname, Aichi|Tokoname]] and by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki Airport) (NKM) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. On [[February 17]],[[2005]], all of [[Nagoya Airport]]'s commercial flights (except for flights operated by [[J-Air]]) moved to Centrair. [[Nagoya Airport]] is now used as a [[general aviation]] and [[airbase]] facility. [[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tokaido Shinkansen]], [[Tokaido Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]], among others. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s. The city is also serviced by the [[Nagoya Subway]]. == Economy == [[Image:Nagoya_uitzicht.jpg|thumb|250px|An aerial view of Nagoya]] [[Image:Nagoya_IdcN.jpg|thumb|left|International design center NAGOYA (IdcN)]] Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya (akin to U.S. automakers being based out of [[Detroit, Michigan|Detroit]]). [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. The Japanese [[confectionery]] company [[Marukawa]] is headquartered in Nagoya, as is the fine ceramics company [[Noritake]]. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area. {{Japanese city | Name = Nagoya City | JapaneseName = 名古屋市 | Region = [[Chūbu region|Chūbu]], [[Tokai region|Tokai]] | Prefecture = [[Aichi prefecture]] | Area = 326.45 | Population = 2,190,549 | PopDate = 2003 | Density = 6,710.21 | Mayor = Takehisa Matsubara | Coord = {{coor dm|35|07|N|136|56|E|type:city_region:JP}} | Flower = [[Lilium]] | Tree = [[Camphor Laurel]] | SymbolImage = Nagoya_CitySymbol.png | CityHallPostalCode = 460-0001 | CityHallAddress = Nagoya-shi,
Naka-ku, Sannomaru 3-chome 1-1 | CityHallPhone = 052-972-2017 | CityHallLink = [http://www.city.nagoya.jp/ Nagoya City] | MapImage = Map Nagoya en.png | ExtraNotes = }} {{nihongo|'''Nagoya'''|名古屋市|nagoya-shi}} is the fourth largest and the third most prosperous city in [[Japan]]. Located on the [[Pacific]] [[coast]] in the [[Chūbu region]] on central [[Honshu]], it is the [[capital]] of [[Aichi Prefecture]] and is one of Japan's major [[seaport|port]]s along with those of [[Tokyo]], [[Osaka]], [[Kobe]], [[Yokohama]], [[Chiba]], and [[Hakata-ku, Fukuoka|Hakata]]. It is also the center of Japan's third largest metropolitan region, known as the [[Chukyo Metropolitan Area]]. == History == The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], and was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[City designated by government ordinance (Japan)|government ordinance]]. The city's name was historically written as 那古野 or 名護屋 (also read as ''Nagoya''), and as the city is located between [[Kyoto]] and [[Tokyo]], it was also historically known as {{nihongo|"central capital"|中京|Chūkyō}}. == Sightseeing == [[Image:Nagoya Castle 01.jpg|thumb|left|[[Nagoya Castle]].]] Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include {{nihongo|[[Nagoya Castle]]|名古屋城|Nagoya-jō}} and {{nihongo|[[Atsuta Shrine]]|熱田神宮|Atsuta Jingū}}. [[Nagoya Castle]] ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored in 1959, though some modern amenities such as elevators were added. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent {{nihongo|Golden Orca|金の鯱|Kin no Shachihoko}} on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines {{nihongo|the Kusanagi sacred sword|草薙神剣|[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]}} one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 [[national treasure]]s representing its 2,000 years' history. [[Image:Nagoya_Tower.jpg|thumb|250px|Nagoya TV Tower.]] Modern attractions include the [[Nagoya TV Tower]] and JR Central Towers of [[Nagoya Station]]. == Wards == Nagoya has 16 {{nihongo|[[Wards of Japan|wards]]|''ku''|区}}: {| |- |valign=top| * [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]] * [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]] * [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]] * [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]] * [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]] * [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]] * [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]] * [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]] |valign=top| * [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]] * [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]] * [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]] * [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]] * [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]] * [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]] * [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]] * [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]] |} == Demographics == As of [[2003]], the city has an estimated [[population]] of 2,190,549 and the [[population density|density]] of 6,710.21 persons per [[square kilometre|km²]]. The total area is 326.45 km². Its [[Chukyo Metropolitan Area|metropolitan area]] extends into [[Mie]] and [[Gifu]] prefectures, with a total population of about 9 million people, with only Osaka and Tokyo being larger. == Transportation == [[Image:Surface Entrance to Shiyakusho Station (Nagoya-Japan).jpg|thumb|250px|Entrace to Shiyakusho Subway Station.]] Nagoya is served by [[Chubu Centrair International Airport]] (NGO) in the city of [[Tokoname, Aichi|Tokoname]] and by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki Airport) (NKM) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. On [[February 17]],[[2005]], all of [[Nagoya Airport]]'s commercial flights (except for flights operated by [[J-Air]]) moved to Centrair. [[Nagoya Airport]] is now used as a [[general aviation]] and [[airbase]] facility. [[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tokaido Shinkansen]], [[Tokaido Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]], among others. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s. The city is also serviced by the [[Nagoya Subway]]. == Economy == [[Image:Nagoya_uitzicht.jpg|thumb|250px|An aerial view of Nagoya.]] [[Image:Nagoya_IdcN.jpg|thumb|left|International design center NAGOYA (IdcN).]] Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya (akin to U.S. automakers being based out of [[Detroit, Michigan|Detroit]]). [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. The Japanese [[confectionery]] company [[Marukawa]] is headquartered in Nagoya, as is the fine ceramics company [[Noritake]]. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area. Nagoya is also known as the birthplace of [[pachinko]]. '''Breakdown of Nagoya's [[Gross domestic product|GDP]] by economic activity'''

{{Japanese city | Name = Nagoya City | JapaneseName = 名古屋市 | Region = [[Chūbu region|Chūbu]], [[Tokai region|Tokai]] | Prefecture = [[Aichi prefecture]] | Area = 326.45 | Population = 2,190,549 | PopDate = 2003 | Density = 6,710.21 | Mayor = Takehisa Matsubara | Coord = {{coor dm|35|07|N|136|56|E|type:city_region:JP}} | Flower = [[Lilium]] | Tree = [[Camphor Laurel]] | SymbolImage = Nagoya_CitySymbol.png | CityHallPostalCode = 460-0001 | CityHallAddress = Nagoya-shi,
Naka-ku, Sannomaru 3-chome 1-1 | CityHallPhone = 052-972-2017 | CityHallLink = [http://www.city.nagoya.jp/ Nagoya City] | MapImage = Map Nagoya en.png | ExtraNotes = }} {{nihongo|'''Nagoya'''|名古屋市|nagoya-shi}} is the fourth largest and the third most prosperous city in [[Japan]]. Located on the [[Pacific]] [[coast]] in the [[Chūbu region]] on central [[Honshu]], it is the [[capital]] of [[Aichi Prefecture]] and is one of Japan's major [[seaport|port]]s along with those of [[Tokyo]], [[Osaka]], [[Kobe]], [[Yokohama]], [[Chiba]], and [[Hakata-ku, Fukuoka|Hakata]]. It is also the center of Japan's third largest metropolitan region, known as the [[Chukyo Metropolitan Area]]. == History == The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], and was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[City designated by government ordinance (Japan)|government ordinance]]. The city's name was historically written as 那古野 or 名護屋 (also read as ''Nagoya''), and as the city is located between [[Kyoto]] and [[Tokyo]], it was also historically known as {{nihongo|"central capital"|中京|Chūkyō}}. == Sightseeing == [[Image:Nagoya Castle 01.jpg|thumb|left|[[Nagoya Castle]].]] Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include {{nihongo|[[Nagoya Castle]]|名古屋城|Nagoya-jō}} and {{nihongo|[[Atsuta Shrine]]|熱田神宮|Atsuta Jingū}}. [[Nagoya Castle]] ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored in 1959, though some modern amenities such as elevators were added. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent {{nihongo|Golden Orca|金の鯱|Kin no Shachihoko}} on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines {{nihongo|the Kusanagi sacred sword|草薙神剣|[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]}} one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 [[national treasure]]s representing its 2,000 years' history. [[Image:Nagoya_Tower.jpg|thumb|250px|Nagoya TV Tower.]] Modern attractions include the [[Nagoya TV Tower]] and JR Central Towers of [[Nagoya Station]]. == Wards == Nagoya has 16 {{nihongo|[[Wards of Japan|wards]]|''ku''|区}}: {| |- |valign=top| * [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]] * [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]] * [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]] * [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]] * [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]] * [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]] * [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]] * [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]] |valign=top| * [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]] * [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]] * [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]] * [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]] * [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]] * [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]] * [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]] * [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]] |} == Demographics == As of [[2003]], the city has an estimated [[population]] of 2,190,549 and the [[population density|density]] of 6,710.21 persons per [[square kilometre|km²]]. The total area is 326.45 km². Its [[Chukyo Metropolitan Area|metropolitan area]] extends into [[Mie]] and [[Gifu]] prefectures, with a total population of about 9 million people, with only Osaka and Tokyo being larger. == Transportation == [[Image:Surface Entrance to Shiyakusho Station (Nagoya-Japan).jpg|thumb|250px|Entrace to Shiyakusho Subway Station.]] Nagoya is served by [[Chubu Centrair International Airport]] (NGO) in the city of [[Tokoname, Aichi|Tokoname]] and by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki Airport) (NKM) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. On [[February 17]],[[2005]], all of [[Nagoya Airport]]'s commercial flights (except for flights operated by [[J-Air]]) moved to Centrair. [[Nagoya Airport]] is now used as a [[general aviation]] and [[airbase]] facility. [[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tokaido Shinkansen]], [[Tokaido Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]], among others. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s. The city is also serviced by the [[Nagoya Subway]]. == Economy == [[Image:Nagoya_uitzicht.jpg|thumb|250px|An aerial view of Nagoya.]] [[Image:Nagoya_IdcN.jpg|thumb|left|International design center NAGOYA (IdcN).]] Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya (akin to U.S. automakers being based out of [[Detroit, Michigan|Detroit]]). [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. The Japanese [[confectionery]] company [[Marukawa]] is headquartered in Nagoya, as is the fine ceramics company [[Noritake]]. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area. Nagoya is also known as the birthplace of [[pachinko]]. '''Breakdown of Nagoya's [[Gross domestic product|GDP]] by economic activity'''

League]] | [[Mizuho Athletic Stadium]],

The city's name was historically written as 那古野 or 名護屋 (also read as ''Nagoya''), and as the city is located between [[Kyoto]] and [[Tokyo]], it was also historically known as {{nihongo|"central capital"|中京|Chūkyō}}. == Sightseeing == [[Image:Nagoya Castle 01.jpg|thumb|left|[[Nagoya Castle]].]] Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include {{nihongo|[[Nagoya Castle]]|名古屋城|Nagoya-jō}} and {{nihongo|[[Atsuta Shrine]]|熱田神宮|Atsuta Jingū}}. [[Nagoya Castle]] ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. The city's name was historically written as 那古野 or 名護屋 (also read as ''Nagoya''), and as the city is located between [[Kyoto]] and [[Tokyo]], it was also historically known as {{nihongo|"central capital"|中京|Chūkyō}}. == Sightseeing == [[Image:Nagoya Castle 01.jpg|thumb|left|[[Nagoya Castle]].]] Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include {{nihongo|[[Nagoya Castle]]|名古屋城|Nagoya-jō}} and {{nihongo|[[Atsuta Shrine]]|熱田神宮|Atsuta Jingū}}. [[Nagoya Castle]] ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored in 1959, though some modern amenities such as elevators were added. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent {{nihongo|Golden Orca|金の鯱|Kin no Shachihoko}} on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines {{nihongo|the Kusanagi sacred sword|草薙神剣|[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]}} one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 [[national treasure]]s representing its 2,000 years' history. [[Image:Nagoya_Tower.jpg|thumb|250px|Nagoya TV Tower.]] Modern attractions include the [[Nagoya TV Tower]] and JR Central Towers of [[Nagoya Station]]. == Wards == Nagoya has 16 {{nihongo|[[Wards of Japan|wards]]|''ku''|区}}: {| |- |valign=top| * [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]] * [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]] * [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]] * [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]] * [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]] * [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]] * [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]] * [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]] |valign=top| * [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]] * [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]] * [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]] * [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]] * [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]] * [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]] * [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]] * [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]] |} == Demographics == One of the earliest [[census]] carried out in [[1889]] gave nagoya's [[population]] as 157,496. It reached 1 million mark in [[1934]] and as of [[2004]], the city has an estimated population of 2,202,111 with a [[population density|density]] of 6,745 persons per [[square kilometre|km²]]. There are estimated to be 945,328 households in the city,which is a significant increase from 153,370 they had at the end of the [[World War II]],in [[1945]]. The total area is 326.45 km². Its [[Chūkyō Metropolitan Area|metropolitan area]] extends into [[Mie]] and [[Gifu]] prefectures, with a total population of about 9 million people, with only Osaka and Tokyo being larger. == Transportation == [[Image:Surface Entrance to Shiyakusho Station (Nagoya-Japan).jpg|thumb|250px|Entrace to Shiyakusho Subway Station.]] Nagoya is served by [[Chubu Centrair International Airport]] (NGO) in the city of [[Tokoname, Aichi|Tokoname]] and by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki Airport) (NKM) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. On [[February 17]],[[2005]], all of [[Nagoya Airport]]'s commercial flights (except for flights operated by [[J-Air]]) moved to Centrair. [[Nagoya Airport]] is now used as a [[general aviation]] and [[airbase]] facility. [[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tokaido Shinkansen]], [[Tokaido Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]], among others. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s. The city is also serviced by the [[Nagoya Subway]]. == Economy == [[Image:Nagoya_uitzicht.jpg|thumb|250px|An aerial view of Nagoya.]] [[Image:Nagoya_IdcN.jpg|thumb|left|International design center NAGOYA (IdcN).]] Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya (akin to U.S. automakers being based out of [[Detroit, Michigan|Detroit]]). [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. The Japanese [[confectionery]] company [[Marukawa]] is headquartered in Nagoya, as is the fine ceramics company [[Noritake]]. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area. Nagoya is also known as the birthplace of [[pachinko]]. '''Breakdown of Nagoya's [[Gross domestic product|GDP]] by economic activity'''

Naka-ku, Sannomaru 3-chome 1-1 | CityHallPhone = 052-972-2017 | CityHallLink = [http://www.city.nagoya.jp/ Nagoya City] | MapImage = Map Nagoya en.png | ExtraNotes = }} {{nihongo|'''Nagoya'''|名古屋市|nagoya-shi}} is the fourth largest and the third most prosperous city in [[Japan]]. Located on the [[Pacific]] [[coast]] in the [[Chūbu region]] on central [[Honshu]], it is the [[capital]] of [[Aichi Prefecture]] and is one of Japan's major [[seaport|port]]s along with those of [[Tokyo]], [[Osaka]], [[Kobe]], [[Yokohama]], [[Chiba]], and [[Hakata-ku, Fukuoka|Hakata]]. It is also the center of Japan's third largest metropolitan region, known as the [[Chūkyō Metropolitan Area]]. == History == The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], and was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[City designated by government ordinance (Japan)|government ordinance]]. The city's name was historically written as 那古野 or 名護屋 (also read as ''Nagoya''), and as the city is located between [[Kyoto]] and [[Tokyo]], it was also historically known as {{nihongo|"central capital"|中京|Chūkyō}}. == Sightseeing == [[Image:Nagoya Castle 01.jpg|thumb|left|[[Nagoya Castle]].]] Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include {{nihongo|[[Nagoya Castle]]|名古屋城|Nagoya-jō}} and {{nihongo|[[Atsuta Shrine]]|熱田神宮|Atsuta Jingū}}. [[Nagoya Castle]] ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored in 1959, though some modern amenities such as elevators were added. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent {{nihongo|Golden Orca|金の鯱|Kin no Shachihoko}} on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines {{nihongo|the Kusanagi sacred sword|草薙神剣|[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]}} one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 [[national treasure]]s representing its 2,000 years' history. [[Image:Nagoya_Tower.jpg|thumb|250px|Nagoya TV Tower.]] Modern attractions include the [[Nagoya TV Tower]] and JR Central Towers of [[Nagoya Station]]. == Wards == Nagoya has 16 {{nihongo|[[Wards of Japan|wards]]|''ku''|区}}: {| |- |valign=top| * [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]] * [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]] * [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]] * [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]] * [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]] * [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]] * [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]] * [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]] |valign=top| * [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]] * [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]] * [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]] * [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]] * [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]] * [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]] * [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]] * [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]] |} == Demographics == One of the earliest [[census]] carried out in [[1889]] gave nagoya's [[population]] as 157,496. It reached 1 million mark in [[1934]] and as of [[2004]], the city has an estimated population of 2,202,111 with a [[population density|density]] of 6,745 persons per [[square kilometre|km²]]. There are estimated to be 945,328 households in the city,which is a significant increase from 153,370 they had at the end of the [[World War II]],in [[1945]]. The total area is 326.45 km². Its [[Chūkyō Metropolitan Area|metropolitan area]] extends into [[Mie]] and [[Gifu]] prefectures, with a total population of about 9 million people, with only Osaka and Tokyo being larger. == Transportation == [[Image:Surface Entrance to Shiyakusho Station (Nagoya-Japan).jpg|thumb|250px|Entrace to Shiyakusho Subway Station.]] Nagoya is served by [[Chubu Centrair International Airport]] (NGO) in the city of [[Tokoname, Aichi|Tokoname]] and by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki Airport) (NKM) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. On [[February 17]],[[2005]], all of [[Nagoya Airport]]'s commercial flights (except for flights operated by [[J-Air]]) moved to Centrair. [[Nagoya Airport]] is now used as a [[general aviation]] and [[airbase]] facility. [[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tokaido Shinkansen]], [[Tokaido Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]], among others. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s. The city is also serviced by the [[Nagoya Subway]]. == Economy == [[Image:Nagoya_uitzicht.jpg|thumb|250px|An aerial view of Nagoya.]] [[Image:Nagoya_IdcN.jpg|thumb|left|International design center NAGOYA (IdcN).]] Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya (akin to U.S. automakers being based out of [[Detroit, Michigan|Detroit]]). [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. The Japanese [[confectionery]] company [[Marukawa]] is headquartered in Nagoya, as is the fine ceramics company [[Noritake]]. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area. Nagoya is also known as the birthplace of [[pachinko]]. '''Breakdown of Nagoya's [[Gross domestic product|GDP]] by economic activity'''

Naka-ku, Sannomaru 3-chome 1-1 | CityHallPhone = 052-972-2017 | CityHallLink = [http://www.city.nagoya.jp/ Nagoya City] | MapImage = Map Nagoya en.png | ExtraNotes = }} {{nihongo|'''Nagoya'''|名古屋市|nagoya-shi}} is the fourth largest and the third most prosperous city in [[Japan]]. Located on the [[Pacific]] [[coast]] in the [[Chūbu region]] on central [[Honshu]], it is the [[capital]] of [[Aichi Prefecture]] and is one of Japan's major [[seaport|port]]s along with those of [[Tokyo]], [[Osaka]], [[Kobe]], [[Yokohama]], [[Chiba]], and [[Hakata-ku, Fukuoka|Hakata]]. It is also the center of Japan's third largest metropolitan region, known as the [[Chūkyō Metropolitan Area]]. == History == The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], and was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[City designated by government ordinance (Japan)|government ordinance]]. The city's name was historically written as 那古野 or 名護屋 (also read as ''Nagoya''), and as the city is located between [[Kyoto]] and [[Tokyo]], it was also historically known as {{nihongo|"central capital"|中京|Chūkyō}}. == Sightseeing == [[Image:Nagoya Castle 01.jpg|thumb|left|[[Nagoya Castle]].]] Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include {{nihongo|[[Nagoya Castle]]|名古屋城|Nagoya-jō}} and {{nihongo|[[Atsuta Shrine]]|熱田神宮|Atsuta Jingū}}. [[Nagoya Castle]] ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored in 1959, though some modern amenities such as elevators were added. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent {{nihongo|Golden Orca|金の鯱|Kin no Shachihoko}} on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines {{nihongo|the Kusanagi sacred sword|草薙神剣|[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]}} one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 [[national treasure]]s representing its 2,000 years' history. [[Image:Nagoya_Tower.jpg|thumb|250px|Nagoya TV Tower.]] Modern attractions include the [[Nagoya TV Tower]] and JR Central Towers of [[Nagoya Station]]. == Wards == Nagoya has 16 {{nihongo|[[Wards of Japan|wards]]|''ku''|区}}: {| |- |valign=top| * [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]] * [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]] * [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]] * [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]] * [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]] * [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]] * [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]] * [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]] |valign=top| * [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]] * [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]] * [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]] * [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]] * [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]] * [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]] * [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]] * [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]] |} == Demographics == One of the earliest [[census]] carried out in [[1889]] gave nagoya's [[population]] as 157,496. It reached 1 million mark in [[1934]] and as of [[2004]], the city has an estimated population of 2,202,111 with a [[population density|density]] of 6,745 persons per [[square kilometre|km²]]. There are estimated to be 945,328 households in the city,which is a significant increase from 153,370 they had at the end of the [[World War II]],in [[1945]]. The total area is 326.45 km². Its [[Chūkyō Metropolitan Area|metropolitan area]] extends into [[Mie]] and [[Gifu]] prefectures, with a total population of about 9 million people, with only Osaka and Tokyo being larger. == Transportation == [[Image:Surface Entrance to Shiyakusho Station (Nagoya-Japan).jpg|thumb|250px|Entrace to Shiyakusho Subway Station.]] Nagoya is served by [[Chubu Centrair International Airport]] (NGO) in the city of [[Tokoname, Aichi|Tokoname]] and by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki Airport) (NKM) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. On [[February 17]],[[2005]], all of [[Nagoya Airport]]'s commercial flights (except for flights operated by [[J-Air]]) moved to Centrair. [[Nagoya Airport]] is now used as a [[general aviation]] and [[airbase]] facility. [[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tokaido Shinkansen]], [[Tokaido Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]], among others. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tokai region|Tokai]] and [[Kansai region]]s. The city is also serviced by the [[Nagoya Subway]]. == Economy == [[Image:Nagoya_uitzicht.jpg|thumb|250px|An aerial view of Nagoya.]] [[Image:Nagoya_IdcN.jpg|thumb|left|International design center NAGOYA (IdcN).]] Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya (akin to U.S. automakers being based out of [[Detroit, Michigan|Detroit]]). [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. The Japanese [[confectionery]] company [[Marukawa]] is headquartered in Nagoya, as is the fine ceramics company [[Noritake]]. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area. Naka-ku, Sannomaru 3-chome 1-1 | CityHallPhone = 052-972-2017 | CityHallLink = [http://www.city.nagoya.jp/ Nagoya City] | MapImage = Map Nagoya en.png | ExtraNotes = }} {{nihongo|'''Nagoya'''|名古屋市|nagoya-shi}} is the fourth largest and the third most prosperous city in [[Japan]]. Located on the [[Pacific]] [[coast]] in the [[Chūbu region]] on central [[Honshu]], it is the [[capital]] of [[Aichi Prefecture]] and is one of Japan's major [[seaport|port]]s along with those of [[Tokyo]], [[Osaka]], [[Kobe]], [[Yokohama]], [[Chiba]], and [[Hakata-ku, Fukuoka|Hakata]]. It is also the center of Japan's third largest metropolitan region, known as the [[Chūkyō Metropolitan Area]]. == History == The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], and was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[City designated by government ordinance (Japan)|government ordinance]]. The city's name was historically written as 那古野 or 名護屋 (also read as ''Nagoya''), and as the city is located between [[Kyoto]] and [[Tokyo]], it was also historically known as {{nihongo|"central capital"|中京|Chūkyō}}. == Sightseeing == [[Image:Nagoya Castle 01.jpg|thumb|left|[[Nagoya Castle]].]] Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include {{nihongo|[[Nagoya Castle]]|名古屋城|Nagoya-jō}} and {{nihongo|[[Atsuta Shrine]]|熱田神宮|Atsuta Jingū}}. [[Nagoya Castle]] ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored in 1959, though some modern amenities such as elevators were added. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent {{nihongo|Golden Orca|金の鯱|Kin no Shachihoko}} on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines {{nihongo|the Kusanagi sacred sword|草薙神剣|[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]}} one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 [[national treasure]]s representing its 2,000 years' history. [[Image:Nagoya_Tower.jpg|thumb|250px|Nagoya TV Tower.]] Modern attractions include the [[Nagoya TV Tower]] and JR Central Towers of [[Nagoya Station]]. == Wards == Nagoya has 16 {{nihongo|[[Wards of Japan|wards]]|''ku''|区}}: {| |- |valign=top| * [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]] * [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]] * [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]] * [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]] * [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]] * [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]] * [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]] * [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]] |valign=top| * [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]] * [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]] * [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]] * [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]] * [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]] * [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]] * [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]] * [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]] |} == Demographics == One of the earliest [[census]] carried out in [[1889]] gave nagoya's [[population]] as 157,496. It reached 1 million mark in [[1934]] and as of [[2004]], the city has an estimated population of 2,202,111 with a [[population density|density]] of 6,745 persons per [[square kilometre|km²]]. There are estimated to be 945,328 households in the city,which is a significant increase from 153,370 they had at the end of the [[World War II]],in [[1945]]. The total area is 326.45 km². The city's name was historically written as the older Emperor of that time(also read as ''Nagoya''), and as the city is located between Kyoto, Shikoku and Tokyo, it was also historically known as {{nihongo|"central capital"|中京|Chūkyō}}. == Sightseeing == [[Image:Nagoya Castle 01.jpg|thumb|left|[[Nagoya Castle]].]] Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include {{nihongo|[[Nagoya Castle]]|名古屋城|Nagoya-jō}} and {{nihongo|[[Atsuta Shrine]]|熱田神宮|Atsuta Jingū}}. [[Nagoya Castle]] ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored in 1959, though some modern amenities such as elevators were added. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent {{nihongo|Golden Orca|金の鯱|Kin no Shachihoko}} on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines {{nihongo|the Kusanagi sacred sword|草薙神剣|[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]}} one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 [[national treasure]]s representing its 2,000 years' history. [[Image:Nagoya_Tower.jpg|thumb|250px|Nagoya TV Tower.]] Modern attractions include the [[Nagoya TV Tower]], JR Central Towers of [[Nagoya Station]],and [[Italia Mura]]. == Wards == Nagoya has 16 {{nihongo|[[Wards of Japan|wards]]|''ku''|区}}: {| |- |valign=top| * [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]] * [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]] * [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]] * [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]] * [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]] * [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]] * [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]] * [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]] |valign=top| * [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]] * [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]] * [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]] * [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]] * [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]] * [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]] * [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]] * [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]] |} == Demographics == One of the earliest [[census]] carried out in [[1889]] gave nagoya's [[population]] as 157,496. It reached 1 million mark in [[1934]] and as of [[2004]], the city has an estimated population of 2,202,111 with a [[population density|density]] of 6,745 persons per [[square kilometre|km²]]. There are estimated to be 945,328 households in the city,which is a significant increase from 153,370 they had at the end of the [[World War II]],in [[1945]]. The total area is 326.45 km². Its [[Chūkyō Metropolitan Area|metropolitan area]] extends into [[Mie]] and [[Gifu]] prefectures, with a total population of about 9 million people, with only Osaka and Tokyo being larger. == Transportation == [[Image:Surface Entrance to Shiyakusho Station (Nagoya-Japan).jpg|thumb|250px|Entrace to Shiyakusho Subway Station.]] Nagoya is served by [[Chūbu Centrair International Airport]] (NGO) in the city of [[Tokoname, Aichi|Tokoname]] and by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki Airport) (NKM) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. On [[February 17]],[[2005]], all of [[Nagoya Airport]]'s commercial flights (except for flights operated by [[J-Air]]) moved to Centrair. [[Nagoya Airport]] is now used as a [[general aviation]] and [[airbase]] facility. [[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tōkaidō Shinkansen]], [[Tōkaidō Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]], among others. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tōkai region|Tōkai]] and [[Kansai region]]s. The city is also serviced by the [[Nagoya Subway]]. == Economy == [[Image:Nagoya_uitzicht.jpg|thumb|250px|An aerial view of Nagoya.]] [[Image:Nagoya_IdcN.jpg|thumb|left|International design center NAGOYA (IdcN).]] Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya (akin to U.S. automakers being based out of [[Detroit, Michigan|Detroit]]). [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. The Japanese [[confectionery]] company [[Marukawa]] is headquartered in Nagoya, as is the fine ceramics company [[Noritake]]. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area. Nagoya is also known as the birthplace of [[pachinko]]. [[Ibanez Guitars]] are based in Nagoya '''Breakdown of Nagoya's [[Gross domestic product|GDP]] by economic activity'''

== Headline text == {{Japanese city | Name = Hong Kong | Country = China Region = [[Chūbu region|Chūbu]], [[Tōkai region|Tōkai]] | Prefecture = [[Aichi prefecture]] | Area = 326.45 | Population = 2,202,111 | PopDate = 2004 | Density = 6,745 | Mayor = Takehisa Matsubara | Coord = {{coor dm|35|07|N|136|56|E|type:city_region:JP}} | Flower = [[Lilium]] | Tree = [[Camphor Laurel]] | SymbolImage = Nagoya_CitySymbol.png | CityHallPostalCode = 460-0001 | CityHallAddress = Nagoya-shi,
Naka-ku, Sannomaru 3-chome 1-1 | CityHallPhone = 052-972-2017 | CityHallLink = [http://www.city.nagoya.jp/ Nagoya City] | MapImage = Map Nagoya en.png | ExtraNotes = }} {{nihongo|'''Nagoya'''|名古屋市|nagoya-shi}} is the fourth largest and the third most prosperous city in [[Japan]]. Located on the [[Pacific]] [[coast]] in the [[Chūbu region]] on central [[Honshū]], it is the [[capital]] of [[Aichi Prefecture]] and is one of Japan's major [[seaport|port]]s along with those of [[Tokyo]], [[Osaka]], [[Kobe]], [[Yokohama]], [[Chiba]], and [[Hakata-ku, Fukuoka|Hakata]]. It is also the center of Japan's third largest metropolitan region, known as the [[Chūkyō Metropolitan Area]]. == History == The city was founded on [[October 1]], [[1889]], and was designated on [[September 1]], [[1956]] by [[City designated by government ordinance (Japan)|government ordinance]]. The city's name was historically written as the older Emperor of that time(also read as ''Nagoya''), and as the city is located between Kyoto, Shikoku and Tokyo, it was also historically known as {{nihongo|"central capital"|中京|Chūkyō}}. == Sightseeing == [[Image:Nagoya Castle 01.jpg|thumb|left|[[Nagoya Castle]].]] Nagoya's famous sight seeing spots include {{nihongo|[[Nagoya Castle]]|名古屋城|Nagoya-jō}} and {{nihongo|[[Atsuta Shrine]]|熱田神宮|Atsuta Jingū}}. [[Nagoya Castle]] ''Nagoya jō'' was built in 1612. Although a large part of it was burned down by the fires of World War II, the castle was restored in 1959, though some modern amenities such as elevators were added. ''Nagoya-jō'' is very famous for two magnificent {{nihongo|Golden Orca|金の鯱|Kin no Shachihoko}} on the roof. They are often used as the symbol of Nagoya. ''Atsuta jingū'' is known as the second-most venerable shrine in Japan. It enshrines {{nihongo|the Kusanagi sacred sword|草薙神剣|[[Kusanagi|Kusanagi no mitsurugi]]}} one of the three [[Japanese imperial regalia|imperial regalia]] of Japan. It holds around 70 festivals in a year, and many people visit the shrine year-round. Also, the shrine has over 4,400 [[national treasure]]s representing its 2,000 years' history. [[Image:Nagoya_Tower.jpg|thumb|250px|Nagoya TV Tower.]] Modern attractions include the [[Nagoya TV Tower]], JR Central Towers of [[Nagoya Station]],and [[Italia Mura]]. == Wards == Nagoya has 16 {{nihongo|[[Wards of Japan|wards]]|''ku''|区}}: {| |- |valign=top| * [[Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Atsuta-ku]] * [[Chikusa-ku, Nagoya|Chikusa-ku]] * [[Higashi-ku, Nagoya|Higashi-ku]] * [[Kita-ku, Nagoya|Kita-ku]] * [[Meito-ku, Nagoya|Meito-ku]] * [[Midori-ku, Nagoya|Midori-ku]] * [[Minami-ku, Nagoya|Minami-ku]] * [[Minato-ku, Nagoya|Minato-ku]] |valign=top| * [[Mizuho-ku, Nagoya|Mizuho-ku]] * [[Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Moriyama-ku]] * [[Naka-ku, Nagoya|Naka-ku]] * [[Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Nakagawa-ku]] * [[Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|Nakamura-ku]] * [[Nishi-ku, Nagoya|Nishi-ku]] * [[Showa-ku, Nagoya|Showa-ku]] * [[Tempaku-ku, Nagoya|Tempaku-ku]] |} == Demographics == One of the earliest [[census]] carried out in [[1889]] gave nagoya's [[population]] as 157,496. It reached 1 million mark in [[1934]] and as of [[2004]], the city has an estimated population of 2,202,111 with a [[population density|density]] of 6,745 persons per [[square kilometre|km²]]. There are estimated to be 945,328 households in the city,which is a significant increase from 153,370 they had at the end of the [[World War II]],in [[1945]]. The total area is 326.45 km². Its [[Chūkyō Metropolitan Area|metropolitan area]] extends into [[Mie]] and [[Gifu]] prefectures, with a total population of about 9 million people, with only Osaka and Tokyo being larger. == Transportation == [[Image:Surface Entrance to Shiyakusho Station (Nagoya-Japan).jpg|thumb|250px|Entrace to Shiyakusho Subway Station.]] Nagoya is served by [[Chūbu Centrair International Airport]] (NGO) in the city of [[Tokoname, Aichi|Tokoname]] and by [[Nagoya Airport]] (Komaki Airport) (NKM) which is located in the cities of [[Komaki]] and [[Kasugai]]. On [[February 17]],[[2005]], all of [[Nagoya Airport]]'s commercial flights (except for flights operated by [[J-Air]]) moved to Centrair. [[Nagoya Airport]] is now used as a [[general aviation]] and [[airbase]] facility. [[Nagoya Station]], the world's largest train station by floor area, is on the [[Tōkaidō Shinkansen]], [[Tōkaidō Main Line]], and [[Chuo Main Line]], among others. The [[Nagoya Railroad]] and [[Kinki Nippon Electric Railway]] provide regional rail service to points in the [[Tōkai region|Tōkai]] and [[Kansai region]]s. The city is also serviced by the [[Nagoya Subway]]. == Economy == [[Image:Nagoya_uitzicht.jpg|thumb|250px|An aerial view of Nagoya.]] [[Image:Nagoya_IdcN.jpg|thumb|left|International design center NAGOYA (IdcN).]] Nagoya's main industry is the automotive business, as many Japanese automotive companies are based out of Nagoya (akin to U.S. automakers being based out of [[Detroit, Michigan|Detroit]]). [[Toyota]] is headquartered in the nearby city of [[Toyota, Aichi|Toyota]]. The Japanese [[confectionery]] company [[Marukawa]] is headquartered in Nagoya, as is the fine ceramics company [[Noritake]]. There is also a sizable aerospace and electronics industry in the area. Nagoya is also known as the birthplace of [[pachinko]]. [[Ibanez Guitars]] are based in Nagoya '''Breakdown of Nagoya's [[Gross domestic product|GDP]] by economic activity'''
(from the 2005 city profile published by the City of Nagoya) *Service 26.5% *Wholesale and Retail 20.2% *Manufacturing 12.3% *Shipping and Communications 10.4% *Real Estate 9.8% *Administrative Services Supply 5.9% *Construction 5.8% *Finance and Insurance 5.4% *Others 3.7% The [[World Expo 2005]], also known as Aichi Expo was held in the eastern hills of Nagoya in the neighboring cities of [[Nagakute, Aichi|Nagakute]] and [[Seto, Aichi|Seto]]. The event was held from March 25 to September 25, 2005. == Sports== Nagoya is home to several professional sports teams: {| class="wikitable" |- !scope="col"| Club !scope="col"| Sport !scope="col"| League !scope="col"| Venue !scope="col"| Established |- | [[Chunichi Dragons]] | [[Baseball]] | [[Central League]] | [[Nagoya Dome]] | [[1936]] |- | [[Nagoya Grampus Eight]] | [[Football (soccer)|Football]] | [[J. League]] | [[Mizuho Athletic Stadium]],
[[Toyota Soccer Stadium]] | [[1992]] |- |} Nagoya is also home of the [[Shonai FC]] amateur football club and Nagoya Barbarians amateur rugby football club. == Sister cities == Nagoya has 5 [[sister cities]][http://www.nsca.gr.jp]: * {{flagicon|United States}} [[Los Angeles]], [[United States of America]] * {{flagicon|Mexico}} [[Mexico City]], [[Mexico]] * {{flagicon|China}} [[Nanjing]], [[People's Republic of China]] * {{flagicon|Australia}} [[Sydney]], [[Australia]] * {{flagicon|Italy}} [[Turin]], [[Italy]] The [[Nagoya International Center]] promotes international exchange in the local community. ===Others=== Also town on [[Batam]] Island, [[Riau Islands]] Province, [[Indonesia]]{{fact}} == External links == {{commons|Nagoya}} * [http://www.wikimapia.org/#y=35150000&x=136910000&z=11&l=1&m=a WikiSatellite view of Nagoya at WikiMapia] * [http://www.nic-nagoya.or.jp Nagoya International Center] * {{wikitravel|Nagoya}} *{{ja icon}} [http://www.city.nagoya.jp/ Official website] *{{en icon}} [http://www.city.nagoya.jp/global/en/ Official website] * [http://www.seekjapan.jp/resources Nagoya InfoGuide] {{Aichi}} {{Regions and administrative divisions of Japan}} [[Category:Nagoya, Aichi| ]] [[Category:Cities in Aichi Prefecture]] [[ar:ناغويا]] [[ca:Nagoya]] [[cs:Nagoja]] [[de:Nagoya]] [[et:Nagoya]] [[es:Nagoya (Aichi)]] [[eo:Nagoja Urbo]] [[fa:ناگویا]] [[fr:Nagoya]] [[gl:Nagoia - 名古屋市]] [[ko:나고야 시]] [[hr:Nagoya]] [[id:Nagoya]] [[it:Nagoya]] [[la:Nagoia]] [[nl:Nagoya]] [[ja:名古屋市]] [[no:Nagoya]] [[pl:Nagoja]] [[pt:Nagoya]] [[ru:Нагоя, Аити]] [[fi:Nagoya]] [[sv:Nagoya]] [[th:นาโกย่า]] [[vi:Nagoya]] [[zh:名古屋市]]
